item.title: Transition‐Metal‐Catalyzed Chelation‐Assisted C(sp2)─H Activation/Annulation for the Synthesis of Seven‐Membered N/O‐Heterocycles
item.description:
Transition-metal-catalyzed directing group chelation-assisted C(sp2)─H activation/annulation strategy is established for the construction of seven-membered N/O-heterocycles. This review classifies the reactions based on [5 + 2], [4 + 3], or [6 + 1] modes and various coupling partners.


This review summarizes the research progress on the synthesis of seven-membered N/O heterocyclic compounds through transition-metal-catalyzed directing group chelation-assisted C(sp2)─H activation, followed by annulation. This review classifies the reactions based on [5 + 2], [4 + 3], or [6 + 1] modes and various coupling partners, covering a wide range of transition-metal catalysts, directing groups, reaction mechanisms, and substrate scopes. It also summarizes the limitations of existing strategies and provides a reasonable outlook for future research directions.

item.title: One‐Pot Synthesis of 7‐(thiomethyl)dibenzo[b,d]azepinones via a 7‐Exo‐Heck/thio‐Michael Cascade
item.description:
A one-pot 7-exo-Heck/thio-Michael addition cascade has been established to construct 7-(thiomethyl) dibenzo[b,d]azepinone scaffolds. Starting from N-(2'-iodo-[1,1'-biaryl])- acrylamide, this sequential transformation generates the exocyclic alkene intermediate in situ and directly traps it with thiols. The method delivers highly diastereoselective seven-membered bridged biaryl lactam frameworks with broad functional-group tolerance.


A practical and highly efficient protocol is developed for the synthesis of 7-(thiomethyl)dibenzo[b,d]azepinones via a sequential 7-exo Heck/thio-Michael addition cascade. This one-pot strategy exhibits a broad substrate scope and remarkable functional group tolerance. Diverse substituents on both the biaryl framework and thiol components are well accommodated, cleanly delivering the target products in moderate to excellent yields (38%–99%) with excellent diastereoselectivity. The scalability and compatibility with cleavable protecting groups, along with successful late-stage transformations, including deprotection, oxidation, and Suzuki coupling, highlight the broad synthetic utility of this protocol for constructing complex heterocycles.

item.title: Red Circularly Polarized Organic Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence From Chiral Perturbation
item.description:
A series of red circularly polarized organic room-temperature phosphorescence (CP-ORTP) materials are developed by designing rigid axially chiral frameworks with heavy-atom decoration.


Here, a series of red-emitting circularly polarized organic room-temperature phosphorescence (CP-ORTP) molecules has been designed and synthesized via a facile one-pot double nucleophilic substitution reaction, which efficiently converts axially chiral precursors into rigid configurationally locked axially chiral frameworks. The resulting organic emitters, incorporating heavy atoms, exhibit red CP-ORTP with lifetimes and phosphorescence asymmetry factors (g Ph) reaching up to 171.5 μs and 3.94 × 10−3, respectively. This work validates the effectiveness of integrating configurationally stable chirality into rigid phosphorescent frameworks as a viable strategy for realizing single-component, long-wavelength CP-ORTP.

item.title: Computational Insights Into the Gold‐ and Palladium‐Catalyzed C─H Arylation of Indoles: Revealing the Origins of Regioselectivities
item.description:
A comprehensive computational study is carried out to gain mechanistic insights into the Au(I)- and Pd(0)-catalyzed C─H arylation reactions of indoles, revealing the origins of different regioselectivity between palladium and gold catalysis.


Herein, a comprehensive computational study was carried out to gain mechanistic insights into the Au(I)- and Pd(0)-catalyzed C─H arylation reactions of indoles with iodobenzene. Initially, the oxidative addition of iodobenzene onto Au(I) and Pd(0) center is both feasible. After the formation of the Au(III) complex, the electrophilicity of Au(III) prefers to bind with C3 site of indoles. With the assistance of base, K3PO4, the deprotonation of the C3─H moiety of indole could occur. Next, a reductive elimination step could follow to furnish the C3-aryl-substituted indoles. The regioselectivity of the Au(I)-catalyzed reaction is mainly controlled by the high eletrophilicity of the Au(III) and the regular tetrahedron configuration of K3PO4. However, for the Pd(0)-catalyzed reaction, the indoles favor to undergo migratory insertion with Pd─C bond and thus leads to the C2-arylation intermediate, from which the corresponding products can be obtained via deprotonation. The higher electron density at the C3 position of indoles promotes its nucleophilic attack on the Pd center during the migratory insertion, whereas the less nucleophilic C2 position becomes the site for aryl group attachment. Subsequent CsOAc-mediated deprotonation at C2 then delivers the C2-arylated product.

item.title: Redefining Metal–Organic Framework Synthesis: An Organic Synthesis‐Inspired Schlenk Route to NH2‐MIL‐125(Ti) and MIL‐125(Ti)
item.description:
This work presents a streamlined, organic synthesis-inspired route for titanium-based metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) using standard Schlenk-line techniques. By eliminating the need for autoclaves and gloveboxes, this method yields NH2-MIL-125(Ti) and MIL-125(Ti) with high crystallinity and photocatalytic H2 production performance comparable to conventional solvothermal methods. This approach enhances accessibility and reproducibility for Ti-MOF preparation.


Conventional synthesis of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) typically relies on solvothermal methods conducted in sealed autoclaves. Moreover, depending on the MOF and reaction conditions, these procedures may also require strictly anhydrous and inert environments, often necessitating the use of a glovebox. These requirements pose challenges for reproducibility and accessibility, particularly in laboratories lacking specialized infrastructure. In this work, an alternative synthetic route for titanium-based MOFs, NH2-MIL-125(Ti) and MIL-125(Ti), is presented. The proposed method eliminates the need for gloveboxes and autoclaves by employing a standard organic synthesis setup based on Schlenk-line techniques. The reaction is performed under reflux in a round-bottom flask equipped with a condenser, under a nitrogen atmosphere and anhydrous conditions. This strategy yields well-crystallized MOF materials with high phase purity and porosity comparable to those produced via conventional solvothermal methods. Furthermore, their performance in photocatalytic hydrogen production is of the same order of magnitude as that of conventionally synthesized analogs.

item.title: Harnessing In Situ Vinyl Azide Formation for the Synthesis of [1,2,3]triazolo[5,1‐a]isoquinolines and a Papaverine Analog
item.description:
A sequential one-pot silver-catalyzed chemoselective hydroazidation of diynes followed by an intramolecular [3+2] cycloaddition reaction provided access to a series of [1,2,3]-triazolo[5,1-a]isoquinoline frameworks. Downstream denitrogenative ring opening led to isoquinolines, including an analog of the potential antispasmodic drug papaverine. Probable reaction intermediates were identified through various control experiments.


“Click” reactions of organic azides with C─C triple bonds for triazole ring construction have been extensively employed in bioorthogonal applications for medicinal chemistry research. We report herein a sequential Ag-catalyzed chemoselective hydroazidation followed by an intramolecular [3 + 2] annulation reaction approach to access a series of [1,2,3]-triazolo[5,1-a]isoquinoline frameworks using TMS-N3 as azide source in good yields. Downstream denitrogenative reactions offer functionalized isoquinolines including potential antispasmodic drug papaverine analog, showcasing the practicality of the current protocol.

item.title: Thermodynamic Prediction of pKa Values of Organophosphorus Compounds in Dimethyl Sulfoxide
item.description:
The Brønsted acidity of organophosphorus compounds is an important parameter for understanding and controlling their reactivity. We present and test a computational protocol targeting organophosphorus Brønsted acidity in DMSO. Results provide a framework for understanding and controlling acid/base properties in organophosphorus chemistry.


Accurate prediction of Brønsted acidity remains a significant challenge for organophosphorus compounds because of their structural diversity and sensitivity to solvation effects. In this work, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were employed to predict pK a values for a diverse set of organophosphorus compounds and additional compounds in dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO). Calculations treated solution-phase free energy differences between conjugate acid–base pairs using the ωB97X-D density functional, triple-zeta basis sets, the solvation model based on density (SMD) continuum model for dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), and a solvated proton free energy calibrated to experiment. Comparison with previously reported theoretical and experimental pK a values demonstrates that the calibrated computational protocol reproduces expected acidity trends across a broad range of molecular scaffolds. The results provide a practical framework for estimating organophosphorus Brønsted acidities with potential applications in organophosphorus chemistry, catalyst development, and materials design.

item.title: Shorter Chains and a Luteolin‐Derived Architecture Favor Intracellular Fluorescence in Oligoether‐Conjugated Flavonoid Fluorophores
item.description:
Oligoether chain length and flavonoid-derived architecture were screened sequentially. Although Q5-TTEG (tetraethylene glycol) emitted more strongly in aqueous solution, the shorter-chain Q5-DEG (diethylene glycol) produced stronger intracellular fluorescence. Among the fully DEG-substituted architectures, L4-DEG combined the highest aqueous brightness with the strongest intracellular fluorescence, identifying it as the lead fluorophore of the series.


Flavonoids offer naturally derived π-conjugated cores for fluorophore design, but limited aqueous compatibility restricts their use in cells. Here we sequentially examine two design variables: oligoether chain length and flavonoid-derived architecture. First, the previously reported Q5-TTEG (tetraethylene glycol) was compared with the shorter-chain analog Q5-DEG (diethylene glycol). Q5-DEG absorbed slightly more strongly in aqueous solution, whereas Q5-TTEG showed higher solution-state emission; in cells, however, Q5-DEG produced approximately 30% stronger intracellular fluorescence in NIH3T3, A549, and HeLa cells, showing that bulk solution emission alone did not predict the intracellular ranking. Retaining the DEG chain, we then compared the luteolin-, quercetin-, and myricetin-derived analogs L4-DEG, Q5-DEG, and M6-DEG. L4-DEG showed the highest molar absorption coefficient in water (2.8 × 103 M−1  cm−1 at 345 nm; λ max = 336 nm), quantum yield (30%), and molecular brightness (8.2 × 102 M−1  cm−1), consistent with the larger inter-ring rotational barrier calculated for its methoxy-truncated model. It also gave the strongest intracellular fluorescence in all three cell lines, while none of the derivatives appreciably reduced cell viability. This sequential screening identifies L4-DEG as a bright, aqueous-compatible fluorophore for cellular imaging.

item.title: Spacer‐Controlled Stability and Solubility of Cysteine Bioconjugates Using a Hydrolytically Stable and Reversible Michael Acceptor
item.description:
We establish 5-hydroxy-1,5-dihydro-2H-pyrrol-2-one (5HP2O) as a tunable cysteine conjugation scaffold, in which N-spacer electronics tune linker reversibility. Electron-withdrawing substituents accelerate retro-Michael exchange, opposite to maleimides, while sodium borohydride reduction eliminates the ring-chain tautomerism and suppresses exchange. Spacer design additionally enhances the solubility of challenging cargoes.


Thiol–maleimide conjugation remains standard for cysteine modification. While non-hydrolyzed thiol–maleimide conjugates undergo retro-Michael deconjugation leading to—usually undesired—payload-loss, recent clinical evidence demonstrates that such linker reversibility in some cases prevents unexpected toxicities. Conjugate stability increases upon succinimide hydrolysis, and its rate is tightly coupled to the electron-withdrawing capacity (EWC) of the N-spacer. We previously introduced 5-hydroxy-1,5-dihydro-2H-pyrrol-2-one (5HP2O) linkers for cysteine-selective bioconjugation. 5HP2O conjugates exhibit full hydrolytic stability but maintain tunable susceptibility to retro-Michael thiol exchange through a ring-chain tautomeric equilibrium. Using model peptides and peptide nucleic acids, we investigate how the modular N-spacer allows tuning conjugate stability and solubility. The rate of retro-Michael reaction correlates with the EWC of the N-spacer and a Taft slope of ρ* =  +0.69 ± 0.05 was reproduced across four independent series. Notably, this correlation is opposite to the one observed for maleimide conjugates. Furthermore, we show that a sodium borohydride reduction step entirely eliminates ring-chain tautomerism, yielding bioconjugates that are inert toward thiol exchange, and thereby obtaining a platform with full control over the linker stability profile. In addition, increasing the hydrophilicity of the N-spacer tuned linker solubility and contributed to the overall solubility of cargoes with challenging solubility profiles.

item.title: Photocatalytic Radical Cascade Polyfluoroalkylation/Cyclization of o‐Cyanoarylacrylamides Toward Polyfluoroalkylated Quinoline‐2,4(1H,3H)‐Diones
item.description:
The visible light photocatalyzed radical cascade cyclization of o-cyanoarylacrylamides for the synthesis of polyfluoroalkylated quinoline-2,4(1H,3H)-diones. This protocol featured with transition-metal-free, additive-free, mild reaction conditions, and simple operation.


To overcome the transition-metal dependence and harsh conditions of traditional syntheses of polyfluoroalkyl-containing quinoline-2,4(1H,3H)-diones, this study proposes a green and efficient visible-light-induced tandem cyclization strategy. This method employs inexpensive Eosin Y as the photocatalyst and sodium tri-/difluoromethanesulfinate as the fluoroalkyl source to achieve the tandem cyclization of o-cyanoarylacrylamides, efficiently constructing structurally diverse polyfluoroalkyl- and perfluoroalkyl-substituted quinoline-2,4(1H,3H)-diones under mild, redox-neutral conditions. Notably, this protocol features transition-metal-free, additive-free, and simple operation, providing a practical new avenue for the late-stage modification of related pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals.

item.title: Derivatization of Amino Acids via Photoredox‐Mediated Decarboxylative C–N Coupling
item.description:
A mild, operationally simple, and stereoretentive dual metallaphotoredox methodology to prepare N,O-aminal precursors of 3-(1H-indazolyl)alanine derivatives, applicable to a range of substituted indazoles. These precursors are obtained with high N1-regioselectivity and are readily converted to the target Boc-protected amino acids via a high-yielding, two-step sequence.


The importance of unnatural amino acids in drug discovery has been further spurred by recent breakthroughs in oral macrocyclic peptides. In this context, 3-(1H-indazolyl)alanine derivatives may serve as valuable bioisosteres of tryptophan and are highly sought after for tuning the properties of peptide therapeutics and peptidomimetics. However, current synthetic routes are often limited by narrow substrate scopes or poor N1/N2 regioselectivity. Herein, we report a mild, operationally simple, and stereoretentive dual metallaphotoredox methodology to prepare N,O-aminal precursors of 3-(1H-indazolyl)alanine derivatives, applicable to a range of substituted indazoles. Notably, these intermediates are obtained with high N1-regioselectivity and are readily converted to the target Boc-protected amino acids via a high-yielding, two-step sequence.

item.title: Optimization of AFAA Synthesis Process for Inhibiting the Formation of Byproduct AAOF
item.description:
AFAA, a key precursor to energetic material DNTF, was synthesized from 1,3-acetonedicarboxylic acid via an optimized two-step route. Intermediates and by-product AAOF were characterized, and mechanisms and yield-influencing factors were identified. Single-factor optimization delivered 87.9% yield (95.3% purity) and 74.5% overall, verified by 10-fold scale-up.


3-Amino-4-(carboxymethyl)furazan (AFAA) can be used to synthesize the high-performance energetic material 3,4-bis(4′-nitrofurazano-3′-yl)furoxan (DNTF). The low yield of AFAA currently hinders the effective synthesis of DNTF. To improve the yield of AFAA, 1,3-acetonedicarboxylic acid was used as the starting material to synthesize AFAA via a two-step route, and the process was optimized. During the synthesis of AFAA, two important intermediates and the byproduct 3-amino-4-amidoximinofurazan (AAOF) were isolated. AAOF was first identified as an AFAA byproduct and mechanistic probe. These compounds were characterized by infrared spectroscopy and nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy. By analyzing their structural characteristics, the formation mechanisms of AFAA and AAOF were proposed. Furthermore, the key factors affecting their yields were clarified based on the deduced formation mechanism. Based on the deduced formation mechanism of AFAA, the single-factor variable method was employed to determine the optimal synthetic conditions for AFAA. Under the optimized synthetic conditions, the yield of the byproduct AAOF was 3.7% (relative to 2-oxomalondialdehyde dioxime), while the target product AFAA was obtained in 87.9% yield (relative to 4-(hydroxyimino)-3-oxobutanoic acid) with a purity of 95.3%. The overall yield was 74.5%. Scale-up experiments at a 10-fold scale demonstrate that this study provides a reference for future engineering applications.

item.title: Conformation and Ionization State Govern Hydrogen Transfer From Caffeic Acid and L‐DOPA to DPPH•
item.description:
Caffeic acid and L-DOPA share a catechol moiety but display distinct reactivity toward 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH•). Experiments and calculations reveal how conformational organization, side-chain conjugation, and ionization govern radical stabilization and reactivity.


Hydrogen-transfer reactions of phenolic compounds and radicals such as 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH•) span a mechanistic continuum from hydrogen-atom transfer (HAT) to proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET), and their character is sensitive to conformation and ionization state. Distinguishing these regimes has relied on spin-density tracking along the reaction coordinate, leaving its electron-density counterpart unexplored. Here, DPPH• scavenging assays were combined with intrinsic thermochemical descriptors and reaction path analyses, following electron-density and spin-density evolution along the intrinsic reaction coordinate, to elucidate the reactivity of caffeic acid (CA), L-DOPA (LD), and the monoanionic form of CA (CAa). CA showed greater radical-scavenging activity than LD. These descriptors indicated that the orientation of the intramolecular O─H···O interaction controls the preferred hydrogen-donating site, while the side chain modulates radical stabilization. Explicit reaction-paths showed that retention of this interaction favored hydrogen transfer, whereas the carboxylate form markedly lowered the computed activation free energy and made the reaction more exergonic. Coupled O─H bond cleavage and N─H bond formation occurred through concerted pathways in all systems. These processes were predominantly HAT-like for CA and LD, whereas CAa showed earlier spin redistribution and greater charge-transfer/PCET character.

item.title: Palladium Dialkyl‐Bis(phosphino) Ferrocene Complexes for Liebeskind–Srogl Coupling Reactions on s‐Tetrazines: Ligand Design for Lowering Catalyst Loading
item.description:
The palladium-catalyzed Liebeskind–Srogl cross-coupling reactions of s-tetrazines proceed efficiently at low catalyst loading (0.5 to 5 mol%) with the decisive assistance of sterically constrained ferrocenyldiphosphanes ligands. This protocol tolerates electron-donating and withdrawing substituents on the (heteroaryl)aryl boronic acids.


s-aryltetrazines are valuable yet sensitive substrates whose cross-coupling functionalization often requires high palladium loadings. Herein, we report the development of sterically hindered and electron-rich dialkyl bis(phosphino)ferrocene ligands for the Pd-catalyzed Liebeskind–Srogl coupling of 3-thio-s-tetrazines with arylboronic acids. The optimized catalytic system, based on a tert-butyl-substituted diphosphane (L2), enables efficient coupling in DMF at 80 °C using Ag2O as a promoter, with catalyst loadings reduced to 0.5–5 mol% (TON up to ~150). A broad range of electron-rich and electron-poor boronic acids is tolerated, affording the corresponding arylated tetrazines in moderate to excellent yields. Structural analysis of the ligand suggests that increased steric constraint and electron donation enhance catalyst stability and efficiency. These results highlight the importance of ferrocenyl ligand design for improving low-loading palladium catalysis in tetrazine cross-coupling chemistry.

item.title: 2,3,6,7‐Naphthalene Diimide Extended‐Pillar[6]arene: A Host for Recognition of Large‐Sized Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons
item.description:
A nanometer-sized macrocyclic host named 2,3,6,7-naphthalene diimide extended-pillar[6]arene was efficiently synthesized and its complexation with large-sized polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons was studied.


Herein, we report an efficient synthetic strategy for a novel 2,3,6,7-naphthalene diimide extended-pillar[6]arene 1, obtained in 42% yield and unambiguously characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis. Host 1 with large cavity can be used for encapsulating large-sized polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, forming 1:1 complexes in solution. Interestingly, in the solid-state external complex 1@G3 can be formed and further stacked edge-to-edge in rows to form ABAB alternating one-dimensional supramolecular polymers.

item.title: Harnessing a Recyclable Choline Chloride–Boric Acid Deep Eutectic Solvent for Sustainable One‐Pot Synthesis of Substituted Pyridines
item.description:
A sustainable, metal-, base-, and solvent-free one-pot synthesis of substituted pyridines was developed using cholinechloride–boric acid DES as an H-bond-driven recyclable reaction medium. The protocol delivers up to 94% yield across 37 examples under mild reaction conditions, with scale-up feasibility, favorable green metrics, and operational simplicity.


The development of practical and sustainable methods for pyridine synthesis has attracted considerable interest owing to the importance of functionalized pyridine scaffolds. However, accomplishing efficient pyridine synthesis under mild conditions using sustainable reaction environments remains challenging. A choline chloride–boric acid deep eutectic reaction medium has been developed for the metal free one-pot multicomponent synthesis of pyridine derivatives using aldehydes, acetophenones, and ammonium acetate. The ChCl–BA medium combines Lewis acidity with a hydrogen-bond-rich environment, providing favorable conditions for the multicomponent transformation and affording a broad range of pyridines in yields up to 94%. The protocol is operationally simple, readily scalable, and allows recovery and reuse of the deep eutectic medium for five consecutive cycles. FT–IR studies revealed interactions between the carbonyl groups and DES, while control experiments provided mechanistic insight into the formation of a 1,5-diketone intermediate. Favorable green chemistry metrics further highlight the practical and environmental benefits of the developed protocol.

item.title: Synthesis of a Tetracene‐Based Helicene
item.description:
A tetracene-based nor[6]helicene was synthesized by the Scholl cyclization of 5-(phenanthren-4-yl)tetracene wherein tetracene is fused with phenanthrene through a pentagon. This helicene exhibited the lowest-energy bands spanning to 670 nm and the corresponding Cotton effect was recorded at up to 650 nm with a maximum |g CD| of 6.1 × 10–3 at 316 nm.


Chiral tetracene-based π-systems have remained largely unexplored. Herein, we report the synthesis of a tetracene-based nor[6]helicene from 5-(phenanthren-4-yl)tetracene wherein parent tetracene is fused with phenanthrene through a pentagon. The electron-deficient character of the pentagonal ring consequently imparts a considerably narrowed HOMO–LUMO gap, leading to absorption edge found at 670 nm. The optical resolution of the tetracene-based nor[6]helicene gave two enantiomers showing mirror-image Cotton effects reaching to 650 nm. The largest absorption dissymmetry factor was recorded to be |g CD| = 6.0 × 10–3 at 316 nm. According to theoretical calculations, this molecule possesses the relatively large magnetic transition dipole moments in most vertical transitions on the ground of peripheral distribution of the electron densities engaged in the magnetic term of the transition dipole moments.

item.title: Electrolyte Enhanced Regioselectivity in the Electrophotocatalytic N‐Arylation of Pyrazoles
item.description:
Electrophotocatalysis (EPC), using a trisaminocyclopropenium (TAC) catalyst in continuous flow, enables supporting-electrolyte-controlled N-arylation of 3-substituted pyrazoles with mesitylene. Zn(BF4)2·6H2O as supporting electrolyte enhances yield and regioselectivity, favoring the N1 over N2 regioisomer. This method delivers up to 93% yield and N1:N2 ratios up to 100:1.


Electrophotocatalysis (EPC), which combines photochemical and electrochemical activation, provides an alternative strategy for direct C–N bond formation under mild conditions. In this study, the regioselectivity of electrophotocatalytic C–H/N–H coupling of mesitylene with 3-substituted pyrazoles was investigated in continuous flow using trisaminocyclopropenium (TAC) as the electrophotocatalyst. Supporting electrolyte screening identified Zn(BF4)2·6H2O as the most effective additive, providing the corresponding N-arylated regioisomers in 91% combined yield with an improved N1:N2 ratio of 8:1 and reduced side-product formation. Application to other 3-substituted pyrazoles showed that the zinc electrolyte generally enhanced yield and regioselectivity, reaching yields up to 93% and N1:N2 ratios up to 100:1 for compatible substrates. These findings demonstrate that supporting-electrolyte identity can modulate both reaction efficiency and N-regioselectivity in continuous-flow electrophotocatalysis.

item.title: One Pot Synthesis of Covalently Linked 14π Triphyrin–18π Porphyrin‐14π Triphyrin Triads
item.description:
A unique covalently linked [14]π triphyrin(2.1.1)-[18]π porphyrin(1.1.1.1)-[14]π triphyrin(2.1.1) was synthesized by condensing b-dipyrromethanyl triphyrin(2.1.1) with pentafluorobenzaldehyde under BF3.OEt2 catalyzed conditions, and the porphyrin unit of the triad was selectively metalated with Cu(II) and Zn(II) under metalation conditions. 1D & 2D NMR, absorption, fluorescence and DFT/TD-DFT studies indicated that the triads exhibit interesting structure and electronic properties.


The first example of a covalently linked 14π triphyrin-18π porphyrin-14π triphyrin triad 4, containing contracted triphyrin(2.1.1) and porphyrin/metalloporphyrin(1.1.1.1) subunits, was synthesized by condensation of β-dipyrromethanyl triphyrin(2.1.1) 2 with pentafluorobenzaldehyde in dry CH2Cl2 using BF3·OEt2 as a Lewis acid catalyst under a nitrogen atmosphere for 45 min, followed by DDQ oxidation under open-air conditions for an additional 30 min. Metallation of the porphyrin sub-unit of free-base triad 4 with Cu(CH3COO)2 and Zn(CH3COO)2 in a CHCl3/CH3OH afforded the corresponding triphyrin(2.1.1)2–metalloporphyrin triads 4-Cu(II) and 4-Zn(II), respectively. The free-base triad 4 and its metallated analogs 4-Cu(II) and 4-Zn(II) were thoroughly characterized by HR-MS, 1D and 2D NMR spectroscopy, absorption spectroscopy, and DFT/TD-DFT studies. These triads represent unique hybrid π-conjugated macrocyclic systems comprising two distinct aromatic frameworks such as contracted 14π triphyrin(2.1.1) and regular 18π porphyrin(1.1.1.1), each exhibiting different electronic and structural characteristics. Electronic absorption and electrochemical studies revealed weak intramolecular interactions between the triphyrin and porphyrin subunits in triads 4, 4-Cu(II), and 4-Zn(II). Furthermore, the DFT and TD-DFT calculations were found to be consistent with the experimental observations.

item.title: Copper Nanoparticle‐Catalyzed Tandem Cycloaddition–Deacetylation for the Synthesis of Glycosyl Triazoles
item.description:
A tandem strategy combining copper-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) and in situ deacetylation enables the direct synthesis of deprotected glycosyl-1,2,3-triazoles from acetylated precursors. The copper nanoparticles supported on activated carbon (CuNPs/C) catalyst promotes both steps in a single operation under mild conditions.


A practical and efficient method for the synthesis of glycosyl-1,2,3-triazole hybrids has been developed using copper nanoparticles supported on activated carbon as a catalyst. The methodology is based on a tandem process combining Cu-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition with in situ deacetylation of carbohydrate derivatives under mild conditions. To the best of our knowledge, tandem CuAAC–deacetylation strategies enabling direct access to unprotected glycosyl triazoles have not been previously reported. The reaction proceeds in methanol at 65 °C using a low metal loading (1.0 mol% Cu), affording a series of glucosyl-, galactosyl-, and lactosyl-triazole derivatives in good to excellent yields. The protocol was successfully performed on a larger scale (1 mmol), maintaining comparable efficiency. This approach eliminates the need for a separate deprotection step typically required for carbohydrate-derived azides, providing a step-economical and operationally simple route to unprotected glycosyl triazoles. A total of thirteen glycosyl-1,2,3-triazole derivatives were synthesized, including 12 new compounds, which were fully characterized by NMR spectroscopy and HRMS. Preliminary biological evaluation revealed promising α-glucosidase inhibitory activity for selected disaccharide derivatives, which outperformed the reference compound. In silico ADME analysis revealed physicochemical profiles consistent with known α-glucosidase inhibitors, supporting their suitability for localized intestinal activity.

item.title: Electrochemical Selenocyanation and Thiocyanation of Azaindoles and Deazapurines
item.description:
An electrocatalytic method for the chalgenocyanation (selenocyanation and thiocyanation) of azaindoles and 7-deazapurines is reported herein.


An economical and regioselective electrochemical oxidative C─H selenocyanation or thiocyanation of N-rich heteroarenes, such as azaindole and deazapurine, is reported utilizing graphite electrodes. The reaction proceeds without the need for any catalyst or oxidant under a constant electric current in an undivided electrolytic cell. The commercially available reagents KSCN or KSeCN were used for the chalcogenocyanation reactions. A variety of selenocyanated and thiocyanated derivatives were synthesized in yields of 70%–90%, and the reactions also tolerated different electron-rich or electron-deficient substituents on the heterocyclic core.

item.title: Regioselective Synthesis of Vicinal Diamines by Pr(OTf)3‐Catalyzed Intermolecular Aminolysis of N‐Alkyl‐2,3‐Aziridinyl Alcohols
item.description:
A Pr(OTf)3-catalyzed aminolysis reaction of N-alkyl 2,3-aziridinyl alcohols provided vicinal diamines with C3 selective introduction of the amine nucleophiles. Aliphatic and aromatic amines were efficiently incorporated, and mechanistic analysis revealed that bidentate coordination of the catalyst to the hydroxy group and alkylated aziridine nitrogen atom is crucial for controlling regioselectivity.


Vicinal diamine motifs are found in a wide variety of bioactive molecules and act as valuable ligands for transition-metal catalysts. Aminolysis of aziridines is a direct and atom-economical synthesis approach to these structural units; however, controlling the regioselectivity of the intermolecular ring opening of nonactivated aziridines remains challenging. Herein, we report a Pr(OTf)3-catalyzed regioselective intermolecular aminolysis of N-alkyl-2,3-aziridinyl alcohols. In benzotrifluoride, various aliphatic and aromatic amines undergo selective nucleophilic attack at the C3 position to afford the corresponding vicinal diamines. Investigation of O-protected and N-protected substrates suggests that bidentate coordination of the lanthanide catalyst to the free hydroxy group and alkylated aziridine nitrogen plays a key role in achieving the observed regioselectivity.

item.title: Thermal Nickel‐Catalyzed N‐Arylation of Sulfonimidamides With (Hetero)aryl Chlorides Enabled by PAd‐DalPhos Ligation
item.description:
The nickel-catalyzed S═NH N-arylation of sulfonimidamides is described, with useful demonstrated substrate scope involving inexpensive and widely available (hetero)aryl chloride reaction partners, including the active pharmaceutical ingredient chlorpromazine.


Reported herein is the first nickel-catalyzed N-arylation of sulfonimidamides at the imine position employing (hetero)aryl chloride reaction partners with useful substrate scope. Such otherwise challenging transformations are enabled under mild conditions and in synthetically useful isolated yields by use of a PAd-DalPhos/Ni catalyst system, including N-arylation of the active pharmaceutical ingredient chlorpromazine.

item.title: Copper‐Catalyzed C–H Insertion of N‐Heterocycles Into Diazo Arylidene Succinimides
item.description:
Cu(OTf)2-catalyzed regioselective C–H insertion of heteroarenes with diazo arylidene succinimides afforded selective C3 functionalized products in good yields.


Copper(II) triflate is found to be an effective catalyst for the regioselective C–H insertion of heteroaromatic compounds into diazo arylidene succinimide-based carbene precursors. Preferential C3–H insertion occurs in N-substituted and unsubstituted indoles, while selective C2–H insertion occurs when the C3 site is blocked. This technique was extended to other heteroaromatic compounds, such as carbazoles, phenothiazines and pyrrole, and all of them yielded the respective C–H insertion products in good yields.

item.title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Thiomethylation of Arenes: A Convenient Method for Molecular Electronics Applications
item.description:
Practical palladium-catalyzed methodology for the thiomethylation of aryl bromides, iodides, and triflates using sodium methanethiolate (NaSMe) has been developed. Optimization of the catalytic system afforded a robust protocol applicable to structurally diverse arenes, with high functional group compatibility and gram-scale performance, providing aryl methyl sulfides suitable for applications in molecular electronics.


Thiomethyl groups (─SMe) are highly relevant in molecular electronics, particularly in studies exploring single-molecule electron transport using the scanning tunneling microscope-break junction (STM-BJ) technique. These groups play a crucial role by acting as anchoring groups for gold electrodes. However, general synthetic methodologies for installing this functional group are scarce. Herein, we present a palladium-catalyzed reaction for the thiomethylation of aryl iodides, bromides, and triflates using NaSMe as the nucleophilic reagent. This methodology is robust, scalable, and exhibits broad functional group compatibility and structural diversity.

item.title: Graphitic Carbon Nitride‐Supported Manganese Catalyst for Direct C(sp3)–H Alkylation of 9H‐Fluorene Using Alcohols
item.description:
A C(sp3)–H alkylation of 9H-fluorene with alcohols through a borrowing hydrogen pathway promoted by a graphitic carbon nitride-supported manganese catalyst is presented. This air-stable, inexpensive, and recyclable catalyst demonstrates excellent reactivity and selectivity toward the alkylation of 9H-fluorene derivatives with different substituted aromatic and aliphatic alcohols.


We demonstrated the C(sp3)–H alkylation of 9H-fluorene with alcohols through a borrowing hydrogen mechanism, employing a graphitic carbon nitride-supported manganese oxide heterogeneous catalyst. This cost-effective manganese catalyst exhibits high reactivity and good functional-group tolerance, selectively producing monoalkylated fluorene in high yields. Additionally, the catalyst is air-stable, versatile across a wide range of substrates, suitable for gram-scale synthesis, and can be recycled multiple times.

item.title: Base‐Controlled Switchable Umpolung Phosphorylation of Tyrosine, Cysteine, and Tryptophan by CHCl3‐Assisted Phosphonium Salt Catalysis
item.description:
A base-dependent umpolung phosphorylation of tyrosine in short peptides has been demonstrated using H-phosphine oxides as electrophilic phosphoryl donors in the presence of DBU base in CHCl3 under phosphonium salt catalysis. The method has been extended to cysteine and tryptophan using Cs2CO3 as a base.


Chemical post-modification of peptides is a powerful approach for enabling structural diversification and rapid derivatization during the development of peptide therapeutics. In particular, tyrosine phosphorylation is a key regulatory mechanism in many cellular functions. Furthermore, phosphorylated tyrosine is a fundamental structural unit present in bioactive peptides and their lead compounds. Herein, we report a highly efficient DBU–CHCl3-mediated umpolung phosphorylation of tyrosine in short peptides using H-phosphine oxides as electrophilic phosphoryl donors in both solution and solid phases. The method shows base-controlled selectivity and is applicable to cysteine, and tryptophan using Cs2CO3 as base. The reaction involves base-promoted carbene generation from CHCl3 under phosphonium salt catalysis to form an electrophilic phosphorus species that underwent nucleophilic attack by amino acids, enabling umpolung phosphorylation through O─P, S─P, and N─P bond formation. Furthermore, the strategy has been successfully applied to biomolecule-amino acid conjugates, yielding phosphorylated conjugates in good efficiency.

item.title: NaIO4‐Mediated Tandem Oxidative Annulation of Aryl Isocyanides With 2‐Alkynylanilines: Access to Indolo[2,3‐b]quinolines
item.description:
A NaIO4-mediated metal-free oxidative annulation enables the direct assembly of indolo[2,3-b]quinolines from aryl isocyanides and 2-alkynylanilines under mild conditions. The method provides 23 examples in up to 92% yield, and a representative compound exhibited preliminary antitumor activity.


A NaIO4-mediated oxidative tandem annulation of aryl isocyanides with 2-alkynylanilines has been developed for the efficient construction of the indolo[2,3-b]quinoline scaffold. Under metal-free conditions in an EtOH/H2O solvent system at room temperature, a series of desired products were obtained in moderate to good yields, with the highest yield reaching 92%, and the reaction exhibited good functional-group tolerance. Gram-scale synthesis also proceeded smoothly to afford the product in 86% yield without the need for column chromatographic purification. Preliminary biological evaluation revealed that representative compound 3o showed an inhibitory effect on HCT116 cell proliferation. The transformation is proposed to proceed through a carbodiimide-related pathway.

item.title: Fluorinated Iminosugar Glycomimetics: Synthesis and Activity as GCase Ligands
item.description:
DAST-mediated deoxyfluorination of suitably functionalized piperidines provided regio- and stereoselective access to fluorinated piperidine and pyrrolidine glycomimetics, the latter arising from an unusual ring-contraction process. Fluorination generally enhanced β-glucocerebrosidase (GCase) inhibitory potency, but lost PC activity toward L444P/L444P mutant cell lines.


The incorporation of fluorine into bioactive molecules is a widely employed strategy for tuning molecular recognition and pharmacological properties. The enzyme β-glucocerebrosidase (GCase), whose deficiency causes Gaucher disease and represents a major genetic risk factor for Parkinson disease, is emerging as a key therapeutic target for both pathologies. We report the synthesis and biological evaluation toward GCase of a small collection of fluorinated iminosugars, together with some non-fluorinated novel control compounds. Diethylaminosulfur trifluoride (DAST)-mediated deoxyfluorination of suitably protected piperidine intermediates afforded the corresponding fluorinated derivatives. Fluorination proceeded with retention of configuration and, if an alkyl chain at C-2 is present, induced unexpected stereoselective ring contraction to fluorinated pyrrolidines. Biological evaluation, including enzyme inhibition assays and ex vivo studies in Gaucher disease fibroblasts, revealed distinct behaviors. Fluorination generally enhanced GCase inhibitory potency provided that an alkyl chain was present, whereas restoration of GCase activity in mutant cells depended more subtly on the overall piperidine substitution pattern and was favored by the presence of a trifluoromethyl group in the N-alkyl chain. Overall, this study identified new high-affinity GCase ligands, including a potent fluorinated piperidine, a fluorinated pyrrolidine generated through the ring-contraction process, and a trifluoromethyl analog retaining the ability to restore GCase activity in Gaucher disease fibroblasts.

item.title: Electronic Effect‐Controlled Visible‐Light‐Driven Tetra‐Arylation of p‐Benzoquinone Using a Phenalenyl–Pyrene Hybrid Photocatalyst
item.description:
A newly designed phenalenyl–pyrene hybrid photocatalyst shows excellent photocatalytic activity toward the direct tetra-arylation of p-benzoquinone under visible-light exposure with controlled reactivity.


A phenalenyl–pyrene hybrid system is presented here as an effective photocatalyst for the direct C(sp2)─H arylation of p-benzoquinone under visible light. This process yields a range of biologically and optically relevant redox-active tetra-arylated-p-benzoquinones, utilizing aryl diazonium salts as radical sources. Additionally, the catalyst facilitates the conversion of tetra-arylated-p-benzoquinones into dibenzofuran-type molecules through intramolecular O─C coupling when aryl groups contain powerful inductive withdrawing groups. This study also provides mechanistic insights into the catalytic reaction and the structural characteristics of the synthesized tetra-arylated products.

item.title: Brønsted Acid‐Catalyzed Tandem Aldol Condensation/1,4‐Aza‐Michael Addition: N2‐Selective Alkylation of Tetrazoles
item.description:
A Brønsted acid-catalyzed tandem aldol condensation/1,4-aza-Michael addition strategy is disclosed herein to achieve N2-selective alkylation of tetrazoles with excellent regioselectivities (N2/N1 > 25:1).


Herein, we disclose a Brønsted acid-catalyzed tandem aldol condensation/1,4-aza-Michael addition strategy to achieve highly N2-selective alkylation of tetrazoles (N2/N1 > 25:1), and the N2-selectivity was unambiguously confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Control experiments verify that in situ generated α,β-unsaturated ketones act as key intermediates, and acid catalysis is indispensable for the condensation and conjugate addition steps. With p-toluenesulfonic acid (TsOH) as the optimal catalyst, this transformation tolerates a broad spectrum of tetrazole derivatives with aryl, aliphatic, hydroxyl, pyridyl, and thioether substituents, and the reaction is scalable to gram scale. This straightforward method employs readily available ketones and aldehydes without the need for presynthesized α,β-unsaturated ketones, offering an efficient and regioselective route to N2-alkyl tetrazoles.

item.title: Organocatalytic Reaction of α‐(3‐Isoindolinonyl) propargylic Alcohols With 3‐Aminoindoles for Construction of δ‐Carbolines
item.description:
A TFA-catalyzed cascade transformation of α-(3-isoindolinonyl)propargylic alcohols with 3-aminoindoles has been developed for the efficient, synthesis of multisubstituted δ-carbolines.


An efficient TFA-catalyzed cascade transformation of α-(3-isoindolinonyl)propargylic alcohols with 3-aminoindoles has been developed for the de novo synthesis of multisubstituted δ-carbolines. This one-pot protocol integrates a series of sequential steps, including dehydration, 1,4-addition, isomerization, Claisen rearrangement, aromatization, and ring-opening, to deliver δ-carbolines derivatives in a highly efficient manner. Notably, this work not only provides a powerful strategy for the de novo construction of these complex polycyclic scaffolds but also significantly expands the synthetic utility of α-(3-isoindolinonyl)propargylic alcohols.

item.title: Investigation of α‐Silylalcohols as Chiral Umpolung Carbanion Surrogates Through Stereospecific 1,2‐Brook Rearrangement
item.description:
Deprotonation of chiral α-silyl secondary alcohols leads to masked polarity-reversed chiral carbanions through stereospecific 1,2-Brook rearrangement. In situ trapping with Weinreb amide electrophiles affords α-hydroxyketones with moderate to excellent enantiospecificity (es).


We report the investigation of the enantiospecific trapping of chiral α-silyl secondary alcohols through stereospecific 1,2-Brook rearrangement of the lithium alkoxide. The reaction proceeds through a chiral polarity-reversed carbanion intermediate that can be trapped faster than racemization in many cases. Weinreb amides were applied as electrophiles to access enantioenriched α-hydroxyketones in good yields and variable enantiopurities. Substituent effect studies showed that product enantiopurity was a function of the rate of electrophilic trapping of the intermediate chiral carbanion, with faster trapping rates affording higher chirality transfer. The chiral α-silyl secondary alcohols were conveniently accessed in high enantiopurity using Noyori asymmetric transfer hydrogenation (ATH) with low catalyst loading (0.5 mol% Ru).

item.title: Front Cover: Nucleophilic Reactions of Cyclobutenones and the Related 4,4‐Dichlorocyclobutenone Derivatives (Eur. J. Org. Chem. 43/2026)
item.description: The Front Cover shows how the nucleophilic reactions of cyclobutenones open a window to an array of compounds. The Review by S. Ntsimango and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/ejoc.70837) describes the products that result from various nucleophilic reactions of cyclobutenones. This is depicted by the question mark over a window of possible nucleophilic products that can form from the cyclobutenone ring.

item.title: Nucleophilic Reactions of Cyclobutenones and the Related 4,4‐Dichlorocyclobutenone Derivatives
item.description:
Cyclobutenone derivates and their 4,4-dichloro counterparts have an uninterrupted attention as useful synthons in the synthesis of complex organic molecules. Their nucleophilic reactions remain underexplored. This review brings attention to these reactions, whose outcome is not straightforward. A similar trend is observed with the proposed mechanisms that are used to describe the formation of the observed products.


Cyclobutenones have uninterrupted attention as useful synthons in the synthesis of complex organic molecules. Much of that interest is directed toward strain-release reactions, a result of the inherent ring-strain four-membered ring exacerbated by the embedded enone functionality in the cyclobutenone framework. Little attention is paid to the nucleophilic reactions of the cyclobutenone nucleus and their 4,4-dichloro analogs. These reactions are often found dispersed in literature, and this review is our attempt to bring these reactions to the attention of the synthesis organic chemistry community.

item.title: Multigram Copper‐Catalyzed Azidodeboronation of Alkenyl Boronates
item.description:
Copper-catalyzed azidodeboronation of alkenyl pinacol boronates provided access to functionalized alkenyl azides. A Cu(OAc)2/NaN3-based protocol gave improved yields and operational robustness compared with the CuSO4·5H2O system, enabling multigram synthesis. Thermogravimetric analysis revealed the stability limitations of the products, and a one-pot azidation—click reaction extended the practical scope to unstable or volatile intermediates without their prior isolation.


A multigram synthetic approach to alkenyl azides based on copper-catalyzed azidodeboronation of alkenyl pinacol boronates was described. The optimized protocol relied on the use of Cu(OAc)2 as the reaction promoter, which provided higher, reproducible yields and did not cause uncontrolled decomposition of the reaction mixture, unlike the CuSO4·5H2O-based protocol reported previously. The method was applicable to β-, β,β-, and α,β-substituted substrates, including those bearing electron-withdrawing groups and saturated O-, N-, and S-heterocyclic motifs. Some alkenyl azides were prepared on up to 21 g scale, and their thermal behavior was evaluated by thermogravimetric analysis. The synthetic utility of the products was demonstrated through the preparation of a substituted pyrrole and 1-alkenyl-1,2,3-triazoles. Furthermore, a one-pot azidation—click reaction protocol enabled the direct conversion of alkenyl boronates into the corresponding triazoles without isolation of unstable or highly volatile alkenyl azide intermediates, thereby broadening the accessible substrate scope.

item.title: Beyond Conventional Chemistry: Unlocking the Potential of Thioamides Through Photo‐, Electro‐, and Photoelectrochemical Approaches
item.description:
Thioamides are stepping out of the shadow of amides! Long constrained by harsh conditions and toxic oxidants, these versatile building blocks are being unlocked by sustainable methodologies. This review spotlights the latest breakthroughs in thioamide activation via photo-, electro-, and photoelectrochemical approaches. Discover how these green methods drive the synthesis of vital heterocycles and other useful substrates, complete with mechanistic insights and direct synthetic comparisons.


Thioamides, as indispensable isosteres of classical amides, feature distinct electronic profiles, unique geometries, pronounced sulfur nucleophilicity, and versatile redox behavior. These characteristics render them highly attractive building blocks in modern organic synthesis and crucial structural motifs in pharmaceutical and agrochemical design. While conventional strategies for thioamide activation typically rely on harsh reaction conditions, elevated temperatures, and stoichiometric amounts of hazardous chemical oxidants or unstable radical initiators, recent paradigms have shifted toward cleaner, more sustainable alternatives. This review comprehensively summarizes thioamide transformation through the lens of photochemistry, electrochemistry, and photoelectrochemistry from 1974 to 2026. Special emphasis is placed on comparing the reaction efficiencies, mechanistic pathways, environmental footprints, and substrate scopes of these enabling methodologies in driving intramolecular and intermolecular cyclizations—such as the synthesis of indoles, benzothiazoles, thiazoles, and 1,2,4-thiadiazoles via oxidative dimerization. By highlighting the generation and reactivity patterns of key radical and radical-ion intermediates under mild conditions, this review outlines the transition of thioamide chemistry into the era of green synthesis and provides a forward-looking perspective on its future applications.

item.title: DNA‐Based Solar Cells: From Supramolecular Engineering to Photovoltaic Devices
item.description:
DNA is emerging beyond its genetic role as a sustainable, multifunctional material for optoelectronics and photovoltaics. Its thermal stability, water solubility, and programmable self-assembly enable interface engineering and green processing. This review examines DNA-based silicon, perovskite, organic, and dye-sensitized solar cells, highlighting charge transport, interface stabilization, chromophore organization, and bio-hybrid devices.


Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), beyond its classical role as the molecule encoding genetic information, is gaining attention as a sustainable and multifunctional material for optoelectronic applications, including photovoltaic technologies. Its distinctive properties, e.g., thermal stability, water solubility, and programmable self-assembly, offer unique opportunities for interface engineering and environmentally friendly processing. This review explores the structural and chemical features that make DNA suitable for optoelectronic applications and examines its integration into various solar cell architectures, including silicon, perovskite, organic, and dye-sensitized systems. Emphasis is placed on its role in improving charge transport, stabilizing interfaces, and organizing chromophores. Emerging directions such as hierarchical nanostructures, biomimetic designs inspired by DNA’s helical geometry, and multifunctional scaffolds for complex nanocomposites are discussed as strategies to overcome current limitations. These advances position DNA as a nanoscale architect for next-generation bio-hybrid photovoltaics, paving the way for devices that combine efficiency, sustainability, and durability.

item.title: [2 + 2]‐Cycloaddition: An Approach to Cyclobutane‐/Azetidine‐Containing Bicyclic Amines and Lactams
item.description:
Cyclobutane- and azetidine-fused bicyclic amines are conformationally constrained, sp 3-rich mimetics of pyrrolidine, piperidine, and azepane, and [2 + 2]-cycloaddition is one of the most direct ways to build them. This review maps the known routes onto the resulting scaffolds—3-azabicyclo[3.2.0]heptanes, 3-azabicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes, related lactams, and higher homologs. Intermolecular routes involve imines, unsaturated cyclic amines, and maleimides reacting with alkenes or alkynes, whereas intramolecular ones rely on “head-to-head” or “head-to-tail” cyclizations of bisallylamines. The coverage extends from methods that already work reliably on a gram scale to open challenges, e.g., unactivated alkenes and asymmetric catalysis.


[2 + 2]-Cycloaddition reactions enable direct access to strained four-membered rings and constitute valuable strategies for the synthesis of conformationally constrained bicyclic amines. Conceptually, reported approaches can be divided into intermolecular and intramolecular reactions. Intermolecular variants most commonly involve imines, unsaturated cyclic amines, or maleimides reacting with alkenes or alkynes under photochemical, thermal, or catalytic conditions. Intramolecular reactions are predominantly applied to bisallylamines and typically proceed through “head-to-head” or “head-to-tail” cyclization modes. This review surveys both reaction classes leading to cyclobutane- and azetidine-containing bicyclic amines, as well as related lactams. Key scaffold families, including 3-azabicyclo[3.2.0]heptanes, 3-azabicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes, and higher homologs, are examined with respect to reaction design, regio- and stereochemical outcomes, and substrate scope. Methodological limitations and underexplored reaction modes are highlighted for further development of the [2 + 2]-cycloaddition-based routes to bicyclic amines.

item.title: Catalyst‐Free Annulation of Sulfoxonium Ylides With Quinone Imides: Diastereoselective Synthesis of Indolines and Dihydrobenzofurans
item.description:
A catalyst- and additive-free annulation of sulfoxonium ylides with quinone imides has been developed, enabling the divergent and diastereoselective synthesis of indolines and dihydrobenzofurans (>20:1 dr) under ambient conditions.


A catalyst- and additive-free divergent annulation of sulfoxonium ylides with p-quinone diimides and quinone monoimides has been established under ambient conditions. This operationally simple protocol enables the switchable, diastereoselective synthesis of highly substituted indolines and dihydrobenzofurans with excellent stereocontrol (>20:1 dr) at room temperature. The transformation exhibits broad substrate scope, remarkable functional group tolerance, and good gram-scale scalability. Mechanistic investigations support a stepwise polar pathway involving sequential nucleophilic addition, DMSO elimination, intramolecular cyclization, and aromatization.

item.title: Contrasting Effects of Macrocyclization and Quinoline‐to‐Quinazoline Replacement Toward Bright Azaarene‐Based Fluorophores
item.description:
Comparison of quinoline (Q)-based monomeric fluorophore, Q-based oligomeric fluorophores, and quinazoline (Qz)-based monomeric fluorophores reveals two complementary routes to increased brightness. Oligomerization consistently increases molar absorptivity (ε), strengthening light harvesting, whereas the Q-to-Qz replacement improves fluorescence quantum yield (Φ F) through donor–(π)–acceptor interactions. Substituent-controlled charge transfer further enables tunable emission and solvatochromism across related azaarene frameworks.


Macrocyclic systems composed of luminophoric units are of great interest for a wide range of photonic applications. Our previously developed macrocyclic quinoline (Q) oligomers exhibited characteristic photoluminescence, motivating us to investigate the origin of their molecular brightness and the underlying emission mechanism. Herein, experimental photophysical analyses and computational investigations of these oligomers and their corresponding monomeric units reveal that macrocyclic oligomerization consistently enhances molar absorptivity without compromising fluorescence quantum yield of the individual Q units. As a complementary strategy, Q-to-quinazoline (Qz) replacement affords more electron-deficient fluorophores that exhibit enhanced fluorescence quantum yields through appropriately configured donor–(π)–acceptor interactions. Qz derivatives bearing strongly electron-donating substituents additionally display pronounced positive solvatochromism, whereas a quinazolin-8-ol motif displayed fluorescence quenching via an excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT) pathway. These results establish two contrasting yet complementary approaches to molecular brightness enhancement: macrocyclic oligomerization increases light-harvesting ability, whereas Q-to-Qz replacement improves emission efficiency.

item.title: Iron‐Catalyzed Tandem Benzylic Oxidation/Betti Reaction: Direct Synthesis of Betti’s Bases From Methylarenes
item.description:
A FeCl3-catalyzed tandem benzylic oxidation/Betti reaction enables the direct synthesis of Betti bases from readily available methylarenes, β-naphthol, and heteroaromatic amines. The protocol generates the aldehyde intermediate in situ, avoiding the need for preformed aldehydes and integrating benzylic oxidation with multicomponent bond formation in a single operation under mild conditions.


An efficient and practical FeCl3-catalyzed tandem oxidation/multicomponent protocol has been developed for the synthesis of Betti bases from readily available methylarenes. Using commercially available FeCl3 as an inexpensive and environmentally benign catalyst and tert-butyl hydroperoxide (TBHP) as the oxidant, a variety of methylarenes underwent benzylic oxidation and subsequently participated in a one-pot three-component reaction with β-naphthol and 2-aminoheterocyclic compounds, affording structurally diverse Betti bases in good to excellent yields. The methodology enables the direct utilization of methylarenes as aldehyde surrogates and eliminates the need for prefunctionalized aldehydes, noble-metal catalysts, ligands, and additional promoters. The protocol features operational simplicity, good functional-group tolerance, and the use of inexpensive reagents. By combining benzylic oxidation and Betti-type multicomponent coupling in a single operation, this strategy provides a practical and atom-economical route to biologically and synthetically valuable heteroaromatic Betti bases and further expands the synthetic utility of methylarenes in organic synthesis.

item.title: Synthesis and Optical Properties of Thiophene‐Fused Phosphetene‐Based Heteroaromatics
item.description:
A thiophene-fused phosphetene derivative was synthesized via an organometallic approach. Using P-ring extension, stilbene photocyclization, and thienyl post-functionalization, a series of π-extended P-heterocycles was prepared. The optical properties were systematically investigated and fully rationalized using computational approaches. This study highlights the potential of these unconventional organophosphorus scaffolds for integration into molecular materials.


A thiophene-fused phosphetene derivative was synthesized via an organometallic approach. Using P-ring extension, stilbene photocyclization, and thienyl post-functionalization, a series of π-extended P-heterocycles was prepared. The optical properties of the new compounds were systematically investigated in dilute solution and were fully rationalized using computational approaches. This study highlights the potential of these unconventional organophosphorus scaffolds for integration into molecular materials.

item.title: Metal‐Free Annulation of 1,2,3‐Thiadiazoles and Pyridinium Thiolates to π‐Extended Dithiafulvene Derivatives
item.description:
A metal-free annulation of 1,2,3-thiadiazoles with a pyridinium 1,4-zwitterionic thiolate provides direct access to aryl-substituted and π-extended dithiafulvenes. The reaction exploits in situ generated thioketenes and offers a conceptually distinct alternative to classical phosphite-mediated DTF synthesis.


A metal-free, base-promoted annulation of 1,2,3-thiadiazoles with a 4-methoxypyridinium 1,4-zwitterionic thiolate is reported as a new approach to aryl-substituted dithiafulvenes (DTFs). The transformation provides a complementary alternative to conventional phosphite-mediated olefination strategies and proceeds through the coupling of thioketene precursors, generated in situ from 1,2,3-thiadiazoles, with a sulfur-containing zwitterionic synthon. The method establishes pyridinium 1,4-zwitterionic thiolates as previously unexplored partners for DTF synthesis and introduces a conceptually distinct annulation-based strategy for the construction of dithiafulvene frameworks, expanding the synthetic toolbox available for the preparation of sulfur-rich π-conjugated donor molecules.

item.title: The Dialkylphosphinoyl Motif: Synthetic Access and Applications in Medicinal Chemistry
item.description:
This review illuminates the overlooked world of dialkylphosphine oxides, once dismissed as stubborn by-products with no practical value. Their renaissance began with the FDA approval of brigatinib, which unveiled the remarkable potential of the P(O)Me2 fragment in modern drug design. We provide systematic analysis of synthetic strategies, accumulated experimental data, and applications, offering researchers a clear roadmap to exploit these powerful motifs in the discovery of next-generation therapeutics.


For decades, organophosphorus derivatives of the phosphine oxide class were frequently regarded as unwanted byproducts of classical transformations and remained largely overlooked by applied chemistry. This perception changed markedly following the FDA approval of brigatinib in 2017, the first anticancer drug containing a phosphine oxide moiety. A key contributor to its properties was the dimethylphosphinoyl group, which enabled strong interactions with the biological target. This success renewed interest in dialkylphosphinoyl fragments and stimulated investigations of their chemical space, physicochemical characteristics, and potential applications in drug design. Although several reviews have addressed various aspects of phosphine oxide chemistry, synthetic access to and medicinal chemistry applications of the dialkylphosphinoyl motif have not been systematically considered together. This focused review surveys representative approaches to compounds containing a P(O)R2 unit with two P─C(sp3) bonds, with particular emphasis on the P(O)Me2 group. It covers the use of secondary dialkylphosphine oxides and dialkylphosphinites as reagents for installing this motif, selected alternative synthetic approaches, and representative medicinal chemistry studies. The literature discussed spans foundational reports from the 1950s to current developments, without attempting to provide an exhaustive account of phosphine oxide chemistry as a whole.

item.title: K2WO4‐Catalyzed Solvent‐Free Synthesis of Urea Compounds From Amines and Carbon Dioxide Under Atmospheric Pressure Using a Silylating Reagent
item.description:
Commercially available potassium tungstate (K2WO4) and N,O-bis(trimethylsilyl)acetamide (BSA), which serves as both a silylating reagent and solvent, enabled the solvent-free catalytic synthesis of urea compounds from amines and carbon dioxide under atmospheric pressure, including the one-step preferential synthesis of unsymmetrical urea compounds.


A solvent-free catalytic system for the direct synthesis of urea compounds from amines and carbon dioxide under atmospheric pressure was developed using commercially available and easy-to-handle potassium tungstate (K2WO4) in combination with N,O-bis(trimethylsilyl)acetamide (BSA) as a silylating reagent. The K2WO4 catalyst exhibited higher catalytic activity than the previously reported NH4VO3 catalyst, affording comparable yields in shorter reaction times. The catalytic system was applicable to a wide range of aliphatic and aromatic amines. Furthermore, unsymmetrical urea compounds were efficiently synthesized in the presence of secondary amines, and high reaction efficiency was maintained on a gram scale. These results demonstrate that K2WO4 is a practical and efficient catalyst for the synthesis of both symmetrical and unsymmetrical urea compounds from CO2 under atmospheric pressure.

item.title: Chemical Strategies in Nanocellulose Production: Roles, Mechanisms, and Perspectives
item.description:
This review systematically elaborates chemical strategies and their underlying mechanisms for nanocellulose fabrication, focusing on four mainstream routes: acid-catalyzed hydrolysis, chemical modification, ionic liquid treatment, and deep eutectic solvent processing. It also summarizes prevailing technical limitations and future prospects, aiming to offer theoretical guidance for green, scalable nanocellulose production.


Nanocelluloses have emerged as promising biomass-based nanomaterials with excellent performance in various fields owing to their abundance, renewability, biodegradability, high specific surface area, excellent mechanical properties, and versatile chemical modifiability. They are primarily produced from plant-derived cellulose feedstocks through mechanical disintegration processes, such as disc refining, ultrasonication, and high-pressure homogenization. However, the mechanical fibrillation methods are usually energy-intensive as many cycles are needed to break down the extensive hydrogen-bonding network and van der Waals interactions of native cellulose, thereby limiting both production efficiency and precise structure control of nanocelluloses. To overcome these challenges, a range of chemical strategies, including acid-catalyzed hydrolysis, chemical modification, ionic liquid (IL) treatment, and deep eutectic solvent (DES) processing, have been developed to promote cellulose deconstruction and enable more efficient and controllable nanocellulose production. This review systematically discusses the molecular mechanisms underlying these strategies and their roles in tailoring the key physicochemical properties of nanocelluloses, including morphology, dimensions, crystalline structure, and surface chemistry. The advantages and limitations of each approach are critically compared, and future opportunities for developing green, efficient, and scalable nanocellulose production technologies are highlighted.

item.title: Tetradentate NCCN Cu2+‐NHC Complexes for Efficient A3 Coupling Reactions
item.description:
Tetradentate NCCN copper(II)-NHC complexes catalyze the aldehyde-amine-alkyne (A3) coupling reactions, providing propargylamines in up to 91% yield with broad substrate scope and low catalyst loading. The practical utility of the system is further highlighted by the in situ generation of the catalysts and the subsequent conversion of a propargylamine product into a tetrasubstituted pyrrole derivative.


Tetradentate N-heterocyclic carbene copper complexes represent attractive platforms for multicomponent coupling reactions due to their strong σ-donating character and structural robustness. Herein, we describe the synthesis and electronic modulation of pyridyl-substituted tetradentate NCCN Cu2+–NHC complexes and their application in aldehyde–amine–alkyne (A3) coupling reactions. Preliminary spectroscopic studies reveal substituent-dependent variations in ligand-field strength and highlighting the tunability of the ligand framework. However, under optimized conditions, the Cu–tL–H complex efficiently catalyzes the formation of propargylamines in up to 91% yield using low catalyst loading in 1,4-dioxane. A broad substrate scope demonstrates tolerance toward diverse aldehydes, terminal alkynes, and secondary amines. Furthermore, the synthetic utility of the methodology is illustrated through the in situ generation of these NHC catalyst systems and the related conversion of a selected propargylamine into tetrasubstituted pyrrolic compound.

item.title: N‐Heterocyclic Carbene/Nickel‐Catalyzed Enantioselective Alkylation of Aldehydes With Secondary Trialkylboron Reagents
item.description:
A highly enantioselective Ni-catalyzed alkylation of aldehydes with secondary alkyl organoborons was reported, affording a wide variety of chiral secondary alcohols with high efficiency and selectivity.


Herein, we present highly enantioselective nickel-catalyzed alkylation of aldehydes employing secondary alkyl organoboron reagents as nucleophilic coupling partners. This transformation provides a straightforward and efficient route to a wide variety of chiral secondary alcohols with high yields and exceptional enantiomeric excess. The origin of the remarkable stereoselectivity lies in the judicious design of the catalytic system, wherein a bulky C2-symmetric N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) ligand plays a pivotal role in steering the nucleophilic addition with superior chiral induction. The robustness of this protocol is further demonstrated by its broad scope of aldehydes, excellent functional-group tolerance, and compatibility with various heterocyclic moieties, rendering it a versatile tool for the construction of enantioenriched alcohol scaffolds under mild reaction conditions.

item.title: Cycloaddition of Isothiazol‐3‐one‐1,1‐dioxides With Azomethine Ylide
item.description:
In the cycloaddition of isothiazol-3-one-1,1-dioxides with an azomethine ylide, the reactivity of the latter was investigated in comparison with conventional maleimide templates. Bromination of the isothiazolone derivatives enabled a second cycloaddition with azomethine ylides, providing access to [3.3.3]propellane derivatives.


The first systematic synthesis of tetrahydro-2H-pyrrolo[3,4-d]isothiazol-3(3aH)-one 1,1-dioxides is achieved via a trifluoroacetic acid-catalyzed [3 + 2] cycloaddition. The protocol utilizes a nonstabilized azomethine ylide generated in situ from N-benzyl-N-(methoxymethyl)trimethylsilylmethylamine and isothiazol-3(2H)-one-1,1-diones. Within the framework of a comparative study on C═O to SO2 isosteric replacement, the reactivity of these substrates was evaluated against traditional maleimide templates. Under mild conditions, the reaction proceeds with high diastereoselectivity to afford cis-fused isomers as racemic mixtures of (3aS, 6aR) and (3aR, 6aS) enantiomers. This method provides efficient access to biologically relevant scaffolds, facilitating further investigations into the bioisosteric potential of the sulfonyl moiety in medicinal chemistry.

item.title: Rongalite‐Mediated C(sp2)─H Methylenation of Imidazoheterocycles: A Metal‐Free Route to Symmetric Bis(heteroaryl)Methanes
item.description:
A transition metal-free, rongalite-mediated strategy enables C(sp 2)─H methylenation, providing a straightforward and cost-effective route to bis(heteroaryl)methanes with broad substrate scope and gram-scale applicability.


An efficient and sustainable protocol has been developed for the methylenation of heteroarenes using rongalite as a convenient methylene source. The reaction proceeds through the in situ generation of formaldehyde, enabling a green one-pot synthesis of methylene-bridged bis(heteroaryl) derivatives. The protocol applies to a diverse range of heteroarenes, providing the corresponding products in good to excellent yields. Furthermore, a gram-scale reaction demonstrated the practical applicability and scalability of this methodology.

item.title: Synthesis of the Epimer of the Cytotoxic Prenylated 2,3‐Dihydrobenzofuran‐3‐ol Isolated From Atractylodes lancea (Thunb.) DC and Dehydro‐Oberoniamyosurusin I From a Common Precursor
item.description:
An epimer of the cytotoxic prenylated 2,3-dihydrobenzofuran-3-ol from Atractylodes lancea is synthesized from methylparaben through an organocatalytic intramolecular aldol strategy. Claisen rearrangement, cross-metathesis, and an unexpected dehydration enable access to dehydro-oberoniamyosurusin I, while theoretical studies reveal an unusual decarbonylative pathway governing Claisen selectivity.


The enantioselective synthesis of the epimer of the cytotoxic prenylated 2,3-dihydrobenzofuran-3-ol isolated from Atractylodes lancea (Thunb.) DC from methylparaben is reported. The sequence entailed a key organocatalytic intramolecular aldol reaction to build the 2,3-dihydrobenzofuran-3-ol core. The 7-prenyl side chain was installed by an O-allylation of the phenol moiety, followed by a Claisen rearrangement of the allyl ether, complemented with an olefin cross metathesis under Grubbs II catalysis. Attempts to invert the stereochemistry of the benzylic alcohol met with dehydration, resulting in the synthesis of dehydro-oberoniamyosurusin I from the same precursor. A theoretical study of the selectivity of the Claisen rearrangement, which entailed an unusual decarbonylation stage, was also performed and discussed.

item.title: A General Palladium‐Catalyzed Synthesis of Thioglycosides and Arylthioethers From Activated Phenols and Ketones
item.description:
A palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling enables the direct synthesis of structurally diverse thioglycosides from protected or unprotected 1-thiosugars and triflates. The method features mild conditions, broad functional group tolerance, excellent retention of anomeric configuration, and good to excellent yields, offering a versatile approach to late-stage glycoconjugation of bioactive molecules.


The development of efficient and stereoselective methods for the preparation of thioglycosides remains highly desirable due to their widespread applications in chemical biology, medicinal chemistry, and glycoconjugate synthesis. Herein, we report a palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling strategy enabling the direct formation of C─S glycosidic bonds from protected or unprotected 1-thiosugars and triflate electrophiles. Using the PdG3-Xantphos precatalyst, this transformation proceeds under mild conditions with broad functional group tolerance and excellent retention of anomeric configuration. The method accommodates a diverse range of phenol-, ketone-, and complex molecule-derived triflates, providing access to structurally diverse thioglycosides in good to excellent yields. Notably, the protocol is compatible with bioactive substrates and enables late-stage glycoconjugation of pharmacologically relevant molecules.

item.title: Enantiospecific Synthesis of 1‐Pyrrolines by Gold Catalysis
item.description:
An enantiospecific six-step synthesis of 2,5-disubstituted 1-pyrrolines from commercially available N-Boc-L-serine is reported. Enantiomerically enriched propargylglycine derivatives undergo AuCl3-catalyzed 5-endo-dig cycloisomerization to afford the corresponding 1-pyrrolines with good to excellent enantiomeric excesses (up to >99% ee) for electron-withdrawing substituents, whereas electron-donating substituents promote partial racemization.


Nitrogen-containing heterocycles are important structural motifs in biologically active compounds, with 1-pyrrolines representing valuable scaffolds due to their synthetic versatility and biological relevance. Herein, we report an enantiospecific synthesis of 2,5-disubstituted 1-pyrrolines from commercially available N-Boc-L-serine through preparation of enantiomerically enriched propargylglycine derivatives followed by AuCl3-catalyzed intramolecular cycloisomerization. The synthetic route provided enantiomerically pure Boc-protected propargylglycine methyl ester in four steps and 35% overall yield, offering an alternative to the chemoenzymatic procedure. Key challenges associated with iodide elimination and racemization during trimethylsilyl deprotection were identified and addressed through optimized protocols. Subsequent Sonogashira coupling reactions afforded a series of alkynyl amino acid derivatives, which underwent gold-catalyzed 5-endo-dig cycloisomerization to furnish the corresponding 1-pyrrolines. Chiral HPLC analysis revealed good to excellent enantiomeric excesses, reaching up to >99% ee. While substrates bearing electron-withdrawing substituents largely preserved stereochemical integrity, strongly electron-donating groups promoted partial racemization under the reflux conditions required for cyclization.

item.title: [Au]‐Catalyzed Synthesis of C2‐Spiroannulated Pseudoindoxyls via Redox Cycloisomerization/[3 + 2] Cycloaddition
item.description:
A concise one-pot strategy has been developed for the synthesis of spiroannulated pseudoindoxyl derivatives from o-(2-aminophenylethynyl)nitrobenzenes bearing N-allyl or N-acryloyl groups via nitroalkyne cycloisomerization/intramolecular [3 + 2] cycloaddition. The cycloaddition generally proceeds with meta-selectivity to afford linearly fused bicyclic systems. Notably, N-unsubstituted methacryloyl anilides undergo ortho-cycloaddition to form a novel fused seven-membered ring, whereas corresponding N-methyl- and N-benzyl-substituted analogs furnished the meta-adducts. This operationally simple methodology provides efficient access to architecturally complex pentacyclic scaffolds.


A gold(I)-catalyzed redox cycloisomerization/[3 + 2] dipolar cycloaddition domino reaction of o-(2-aminophenylethynyl)nitrobenzenes (having either N-allyl or N-acryloyl group) has been explored to furnish a diverse array of complex tetrahydroquinoline/“dihydroquinolin-2-one” spiroannulated pseudoindoxyl scaffolds. The in situ intramolecular cycloaddition with the N-ally derivatives was facile, giving the requisite polyheterocyclic products in good-to-excellent yields.
