On the other hand, the same reaction cascade with corresponding N-acryloyl derivatives gave the requisite cycloaddition products in moderate yields. In general, the cycloaddition proceeded exclusively with meta-regioselectivity, resulting in the linearly fused derivatives. Interestingly, in case of NH-methacryloyl derivatives, the cycloaddition resulted in ortho-selectivity, giving the corresponding bridged [4,2,1]-bicyclo derivatives in moderate yields.

item.title: Photoredox/Nickel Dual‑Catalyzed Decarboxylative Cross‑Coupling: Modular Synthesis of 3‑Acylindoles
item.description:
Herein, we report a visible-light photoredox/Ni dual-catalytic decarboxylative coupling of air-stable 3-indolyl α-keto acids with aryl iodides, delivering 3-acylindoles under mild conditions with excellent functional-group tolerance and enabling late-stage acylation. Mechanistic studies support a radical pathway involving an indole-3-formyl radical and a Ni(I)/Ni(III) cycle, providing a robust platform for heterocyclic library synthesis and drug discovery.


This study reports a visible-light-driven photoredox/nickel dual catalytic system for the decarboxylative coupling of 3-indolyl-α-keto acids with aryl iodides, enabling the efficient synthesis of structurally diverse 3-acylindoles. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions without preactivation of substrates, exhibits excellent functional group tolerance including halides and sensitive moieties, and is applicable to the late-stage acylation of bioactive molecules and drug-like fragments. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the reaction is initiated by single-electron oxidation of the 3-indolyl-α-keto acid, generating an indole-3-carbonyl radical, which is subsequently captured by a Ni(0) species and enters a Ni(I)/Ni(III) catalytic cycle. The utilization of air-stable and readily available starting materials, combined with operational simplicity, renders this method a practical and versatile tool for medicinal chemistry and the structural diversification of complex molecules.

item.title: Three‐Component Regiodivergent Carboamination of Fluorinated Dienes
item.description:
Fluorinated 1,3-dienes proved to be a valuable alternative to gem-difluorocyclopropanes as precursors of biologically valuable 1,3-disubsituted 2-fluoroallylic scaffolds. Palladium-catalyzed three-component carboamination afforded 1,2- or 1,4-addition products with a high level of regiodivergence depending on the ligand.


Fluorinated 1,3-dienes proved to be a valuable alternative to gem-difluorocyclopropanes as precursors of biologically valuable 1,3-disubstituted 2-fluoroallylic scaffolds. Palladium-catalyzed three-component carboamination afforded 1,2- or 1,4-addition products with a high level of regiodivergence depending on the ligand.

item.title: Retraction: Pd(II)‐Catalyzed Conversion of N‐Troponyl‐Amino Acid Derivatives Into Cationic Troponyl‐Oxazolidines
item.description: European Journal of Organic Chemistry, EarlyView.

item.title: Synthesis of Diversely Decorated and Stereodefined 4‐Thiomethyl‐β‐Lactams via 4‐Hydroxymethyl‐ and 4‐Bromomethyl‐Substituted Key Intermediates
item.description:
Many antibiotics contain sulfur. In this work, the construction of 3-amino-4-thiomethyl-β-lactams was explored. To that end, hydroxymethyl- and bromomethyl-β-lactam key intermediates were deployed to afford novel thiomethylated azetidin-2-ones with diverse S-substituents and defined configurations. Further transformations yielded NH-β-lactams and thiazolylmethoxyimino derivatives as potential antibacterial agent templates.


Many renowned antibiotics, especially bicyclic β-lactam-based representatives, accommodate one or more sulfur atoms in their structure. In this work, the much less explored class of monocyclic β-lactams was selected as a basis for the construction of unprecedented 3-amino-4-thiomethyl-β-lactams, in which a sulfur substituent is connected to the β-lactam ring via a methylene bridge. To that end, two pathways using different key intermediates, i.e., 4-hydroxymethyl- and 4-bromomethyl-β-lactam systems, were explored. Both approaches enabled the successful preparation of a set of novel thiomethylated azetidin-2-ones, featuring different S-substituents and a well-defined (relative and/or absolute) configuration. Moreover, further processing demonstrated the possibility to convert these scaffolds into either NH-β-lactams or 2-amino-4-thiazolylmethoxyimino-based derivatives. Thus, these new structures can be considered as eligible platform molecules for further elaboration in the context of antibacterial agent development.

item.title: Tandem Michael–Aldol Assembly and Regioselective Aminohydroxylation of a Chlorinated Bicyclo[3.3.1]nonane Core Toward Gymnastatin G
item.description:
A concise strategy for constructing the chlorinated bicyclo[3.3.1]nonane core of gymnastatin G is described. A one-pot Michael–Aldol cascade rapidly assembles the congested framework, followed by regio- and diastereoselective aminohydroxylation using electronically tuned N-oxycarbamates to install a 1,2-amino alcohol motif.


An efficient and regioselective synthetic approach to the chlorinated bicyclo[3.3.1]nonane core of gymnastatin G is described. The densely functionalized bicyclic framework was assembled via a one-pot Michael–Aldol cascade followed by silyl protection, enabling simultaneous construction of the bridged skeleton and installation of a bridgehead quaternary chloride with high diastereoselectivity (ca. 9:1 dr). Late-stage functionalization of the sterically congested bicyclic alkene was achieved through regioselective aminohydroxylation, in which the electronic nature of the N-oxycarbamate reagent played a critical role in promoting nitrogen incorporation. Systematic variation of the arylsulfonyl group revealed that electron-deficient substituents significantly enhance reactivity. Attempts to access the corresponding lactone via Baeyer–Villiger rearrangement toward gymnastatin G were unsuccessful, even after modification of the C9 carbonyl, highlighting pronounced steric and stereoelectronic constraints inherent to the rigid [3.3.1] framework. These findings provide insight into the reactivity and functionalization limits of highly substituted bicyclo[3.3.1] systems and offer guidance for future synthetic efforts toward gymnastatin-type natural products.

item.title: POCl3/Sulfoxide‐ and Acetyl Bromide/Sulfoxide‐Promoted Oxidative Sulfenylation of Indoles
item.description:
A mild and rapid chemoselective sulfenylation of indoles with thiophenols has been established by the use of a sulfoxide oxidant and phosphorus(V) oxychloride or acetyl bromide as an activator at ambient temperature.


A mild and rapid chemoselective sulfenylation of indoles with thiophenols has been established by the employment of sulfoxide as the oxidant and POCl3 (phosphorus oxychloride) or AcBr (acetyl bromide) as the activator at ambient temperature. Sulfenylation of indoles at the C3 position can be achieved in the presence of POCl3 and tetramethylene sulfoxide, while a sulfenylation/bromination cascade was reached by combining AcBr and dimethyl sulfoxide in the reaction system.

item.title: Helical Dinaphthothiophenes Reveal the Limits of BN‐Based Optical Tuning
item.description:
A BN-7-thia[5]helicene and an analogous CC-7-thia[5]helicene were prepared in two efficient synthetic routes. Their geometrical structures barely differ, which allows us to judge the influence of the BN substitution on the electronic properties.


The formal substitution of carbon–carbon (CC) units by boron–nitrogen (BN) units is an established strategy to improve the optical properties of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons while retaining their geometries. We report an example of such a substitution in a 7-thia[5]helicene, which led to almost the same geometry. Although the absorption and fluorescence spectra are alike, BN substitution did not improve the fluorescence quantum yield, which is atypical. Both compounds mostly undergo nonradiative decay pathways, which can be attributed to their helical structure and the heavy-atom-effect of the sulfur atom. Compared to the sulfur-free [5]helicene, racemization occurs very fast at ambient temperature. The molecules demonstrate the limits of BN substitution in improving the optical properties of (thia)helicenes.

item.title: Main Group Acetylides in Copper(I)‐Catalyzed Azide–Alkyne Cycloaddition (CuAAC)
item.description:
All stable acetylides of the main group have been evaluated in copper-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC), and the competency with which they perform in CuAAC correlated with each main group element’s ability to perturb the electronics of its pendant alkyne, as evinced by infrared spectroscopy. Tin acetylides are identified as novel and competent substrates in CuAAC.


We report a systematic evaluation of 23 main group (MG) acetylides (Groups 13–17) in CuAAC, confirming prior MG acetylide reports and identifying tin acetylides as novel competent substrates in CuAAC. Optimized protocols for the corresponding triazolides were developed, and 1,4-regioselectivity was confirmed by single-crystal X-ray crystallography. Infrared spectroscopic analysis revealed that alkyne C≡C stretching frequencies decrease systematically upon descending any group, consistent with back-donation from the heteroatom into the alkyne π*-orbital and increased electron density at the β-carbon—features we propose are prerequisites for productive CuAAC. Acetylides of lighter elements (Si, Ge, B) undergo protonolysis under the reaction conditions rather than cycloaddition. Collectively, these results identify metal-like polarizability as the key criterion governing MG acetylide reactivity in CuAAC and provide a spectroscopic handle for predicting the behavior of heteroatom-substituted alkynes in this reaction.

item.title: Acid‐Promoted Divergent and Chemoselective Annulation of 2‐(Methylthio)‐2‐Thioxoacetates for the Synthesis of 4‐Oxo‐3,4‐Dihydroquinazolines and 4‐Oxo‐4H‐Benzo[d][1,3]thiazines
item.description:
A Brønsted acid-promoted divergent and chemoselective annulation of alkyl/arylmethyl 2 (methylthio)-2-thioxoacetate with 2-aminobenzamides provides efficient access to quinazolinones and benzothiazinones from common precursors. Product selectivity is controlled by the reaction medium under transition metal-free conditions, enabling broad substrate scope and excellent chemoselectivity.


A divergent and chemoselective method to quinazolinones and benzothiazinones has been developed through the reaction of alkyl/arylmethyl 2-(methylthio)-2-thioxoacetate with 2-aminobenzamides under Brønsted acid catalysis. The reaction delivered two structurally distinct heterocyclic scaffolds under different reaction conditions from a common synthetic precursor. The use of p-toluenesulfonic acid (p-TSA) in DMF afforded quinazolinone derivatives in good yields, while reactions performed in an AcOH/DMF (1:1) medium produced the corresponding benzothiazinones with excellent chemoselectivity. The methods demonstarte broad applicability under transition metal-free conditions. The structures and chemoselective cyclization of representative products were unequivocally furnished by spectroscopic characterization and single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis.

item.title: Indole‐ and Benzofuran‐Thioglycoside Synthesis via Palladium‐Catalyzed Migita/Larock Couplings: Synthesis and Photophysical Investigations
item.description:
A Pd-catalyzed Migita/Larock cross-coupling approach allows an efficient synthesis of indole- and benzofuran-thioglycosides as a new chemical space. Our synthetic strategy relies on the use of a 4-iodophenylethynyl motif as a bifunctional platform, enabling the sequential introduction of the glycosyl thiol moiety through a Pd-catalyzed C–S cross-coupling and the indole fragment via a Larock indole synthesis.


An efficient catalytic approach for the synthesis of novel indole- and benzofuran-thioglycoside derivatives by using simple cross-coupling reactions is established. The strategy involves two Pd-catalyzed cross-couplings including C─S bond-forming reaction between glycosyl thiols and p-iodoalkyne, followed by a Larock reaction. Following this catalytic approach, various indole- and benzofuran-containing thioglycoside derivatives were prepared with moderate to good yields (54%–84%). Among all thioglycoside derivatives synthesized, the fully acetylated N-Ts indole-derivative exhibits cytotoxicity against the human colon cancer cell line (HCT116) with an IC50 at the micromolecular level (6.94 ± 0.94 μM). Furthermore, the photophysical properties of all thioglycoside derivatives are studied.

item.title: Arylacetonitrile Meets Benzyl Bromide: Isothiouronium‐Mediated α‐Olefination Strategy for 2,3‐Diarylacrylonitriles
item.description:
Herein, we present an attractive strategy for the synthesis of (Z)-2,3-diarylacrylonitrile derivatives by acceptorless cross-dehydrogenative coupling between arylacetonitrile and benzyl bromide through isothiouronium salts. This α-olefination method is operationally simple and proceeds under open-air, metal-free conditions. With a broader substrate scope and high product yields, the developed protocol offers a useful strategy for synthesizing acrylonitrile derivatives for further academic and industrial exploration.


2,3-Diphenylacrylonitriles are widely used in synthetic and medicinal chemistry and have attracted considerable attention for their accessibility. Their synthetic approaches primarily employ metal-catalyzed coupling reactions between arylacetonitriles and alcohols. Herein, we present an attractive strategy for the synthesis of (Z)-2,3-diarylacrylonitrile derivatives by acceptorless cross-dehydrogenative coupling between arylacetonitrile and benzyl bromide through isothiouronium salts. This α-olefination method is operationally simple and proceeds under open-air, metal-free conditions. With a broader substrate scope and high product yields, the developed protocol offers a useful strategy for synthesizing acrylonitrile derivatives for further academic and industrial exploration.

item.title: Two‐Phase Electrochemical Vicinal Dibromination of Alkenes With Sodium Bromide as the Bromine Source and Supporting Electrolyte
item.description:
An efficient and concise method for two-phase electrochemical vicinal dibromination of alkenes using NaBr as a bromine source and electrolyte under mild, catalyst-free green conditions has been developed.


An environmentally friendly two-phase electrochemical method for the vicinal dibromination of alkenes has been developed. This strategy utilizes inexpensive sodium bromide as both the bromine source and the supporting electrolyte without the use of catalysts, external oxidants, and strong acids. It features simple operation, mild reaction conditions, broad substrate scope, and high efficiency, affording the desired products in up to 97% yield.

item.title: Enantioselective Conjugate Addition of Malononitriles to Enynes: A Stereodivergent Approach to Chiral Allenes
item.description:
Quinine-catalyzed enantioselective conjugate addition of malononitrile derivatives to enynes provides trisubstituted chiral allenes in good to excellent yields and high enantiopurities under mild conditions. Broad substrate scope, easy scalability, and versatile post-synthetic transformations into enantioenriched pyrazoles and furans highlight the synthetic utility of this methodology.


Quinine-catalyzed enantioselective conjugate addition of malononitrile derivatives to enynes enables stereodivergent synthesis of trisubstituted chiral allenes. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions with good to excellent yields and high enantiomeric purities for both diastereoisomers. Optimization revealed that solvent and temperature strongly influence reactivity and stereochemical outcome. A broad range of aromatic and aliphatic enynes, as well as α-substituted malononitriles, are well tolerated. The method is amenable to scale-up and allows efficient derivatization of the resulting allenes into enantioenriched pyrazoles and furans, providing versatile building blocks for asymmetric synthesis.

item.title: Efficient Synthesis of Cannabinoid Acids
item.description:
In this study, an alternative synthesis of cannabinoid acids was developed based on an O→C acyl rearrangement. Specifically, this strategy involved regioselective bromination followed by halogen–lithium exchange and intramolecular nucleophilic addition, which led to successful carboxylation.


Cannabinoid acids are the carboxylic acid precursors of cannabinoids, which are present in high abundance in fresh cannabis plants. During heating and storage, cannabinoid acids undergo decarboxylation to produce the corresponding cannabinoids. Cannabinoid acids have been prepared through the reaction of cannabinoids with methyl magnesium carbonate (MMC); however, this method has a limited substrate scope, and Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinolic acid cannot be produced using this approach. In this study, an alternative synthesis of cannabinoid acids was developed based on an O→C acyl rearrangement. Specifically, this strategy involved regioselective bromination followed by halogen–lithium exchange and intramolecular nucleophilic addition, which led to successful carboxylation. The key reaction was identified as a regioselective bromination using cyclopentyl methyl ether as the optimal solvent, affording the 2-brominated product in high yield. This rearrangement strategy enabled the efficient synthesis of cannabinoid acids from cannabinoids.

item.title: Spring‐Loaded p‐Block Ions: Homodesmotic Ring Strain Energy Benchmarks for Charged Three‐Membered Rings
item.description:
Accurate RSE (ring strain energies) are reported for saturated ionic three-membered rings involving one charged heteroelement of groups 13, 15, 16, or 17, after a thorough study for evaluating the most reliable set of homodesmotic reactions. RSE trends along the groups, periods, and hybridization state of the heteroelement are analyzed. RSE are also dissected into additive strain contributions of atoms and bonds.


Ring strain energy (RSE) is central to the stability and ring-opening chemistry of three-membered rings (3MRs), yet reliable benchmarks for ionic p-block 3MRs remain scarce. Here, we establish a unified homodesmotic protocol for charged saturated 3MRs: monocationic pnictogeniranium, chalcogeniranium and halonium ions, and monoanionic trieliranides bearing H, F, or Me ligands. A three-tier workflow, from GFN2-xTB screening to DLPNO-CCSD(T)/def2-QZVPP refinement, is used to compare counter-ion-free reactions, Coulomb-corrected charge-separated products and explicit ion pairs with SbF6 − or Cs+. Benchmarking shows that naked-ion C─C cleavage, or the average of naked-ion C─C and C─El cleavages where appropriate, gives the most transferable RSE scale while avoiding artifacts from ion pairing. Cationic 3MRs are generally more strained than their neutral analogs, whereas trieliranides show stronger substituent control, with fluorination markedly increasing RSE. The heaviest pnictogeniranium cations (As, Sb, Bi) are best described as pseudocyclic, nonclassical multicentre C2Pn frameworks lacking an RCP and displaying Dewar–Chatt–Duncanson-type structures. Periodic trends are rationalized through lone-pair-driven hybridization changes and charge-dependent bonding. Additive atom and bond strain contributions are reported to enable rapid estimation of RSE in charged p-block 3MRs.

item.title: Copper(II)/4‐Dimethylaminopyridine‐Mediated Oxidative Cyclization in Low‐Melting Mixtures: Access to Cyclopropane‐Fused Aza‐Heterocycles
item.description:
Therapeutically important 3-azabicyclo[n.1.0]alkanes were prepared from readily accessible N-allyl/homoallyl-malonamates by oxidative cyclization, involving single-electron transfer, in a deep eutectic solvent. The protocol was extended to active methylene amides, including phenylsulfonylacetamide, to access cyclopropane-fused aza-heterocycles, and the strategy enabled the concise synthesis of the antidepressant drug candidate GSK1360707.


A simple and efficient one-pot approach has been developed for the stereoselective synthesis of 3-azabicyclo[n.1.0]alkane derivatives, employing a low–melting mixture (LMM) composed of choline chloride (ChCl) and N,N-dimethylurea (DMU). This green and sustainable protocol facilitates the intramolecular oxidative cyclization of N-allyl malonamates to afford a diverse array of cyclopropane-fused aza-heterocycles in excellent yields. Furthermore, the utility of this methodology is exemplified in the concise and efficient synthesis of the antidepressant drug candidate GSK1360707.

item.title: Visible‐Light‐Driven Regioselective Cross‐Dehydrogenative C–H Thio‐ and Selenocyanation of Indolo[1,2‐a]quinoxalines Under Photocatalyst‐, Oxidant‐ and Metal‐Free Aerobic Conditions
item.description:
An atom-economical, functional-group-tolerant method is reported for the visible-light-mediated thio- and selenocyanation of a variety of indoloquinoxalines under aerobic conditions at ambient temperature.


A visible-light-promoted cross-dehydrogenative protocol has been developed for the regioselective thiocyanation and selenocyanation of indolo[1,2-a]quinoxaline derivatives. This photoinduced transformation proceeds at ambient temperature under metal-free aerobic conditions without using an external oxidant and any photosensitizer. The key features of this protocol, including high yields, excellent regioselectivity, operational simplicity, broad functional group tolerance, and scalability, make it a synthetically attractive and practical method.

item.title: Synthesis of Flavones by Intramolecular O‐Arylation of Unactivated Halogenated Aryl‐1,3‐diketones
item.description:
A protocol for the synthesis of flavone derivatives starting from mono- and dihalogenated diketones including fluorinated derivatives in a very simple and effective way is reported.


Flavones are an important class of secondary metabolites in plants. Here we report a straightforward method for the conversion of unactivated halogenated 1,3-biaryl-1,3-diketones into chromenone derivatives via intramolecular O-arylation under mild conditions. The resulting flavones were obtained in excellent to moderate yields. The synthesis typically proceeds according to a SNAr mechanism under basic conditions without the requirement of any expensive catalyst. After successful implementation of fluorinated aryl diketones which lead to so far inaccessible fluoro-substituted flavones, the scope of the reaction was also extended to chlorinated and brominated substrates as well as to substances with electron-withdrawing or -donating substituents to demonstrate the functional group tolerance of the method. As an inverted reactivity was observed for bromo-chloro diketones, quantum chemical calculations have been applied to support the proposed concerted mechanism (cSNAr) for this case.

item.title: Direct Synthesis of α‐Amino Ketones From Aldehydes and Amines via Photocatalytic In Situ Imines Hydroacylation
item.description:
A hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) photocatalytic approach has been developed for the direct synthesis of α-amino ketones from aldehydes and amines, featuring high atom- and step-economy, simple operation, good sustainability, and better practicality.


α-Amino ketones have essential applications in pharmaceuticals and organic synthesis. The hydroacylation of imines is an attractive approach to access such valuable compounds. However, existing methods for hydroacylation with readily available aldehydes are highly dependent on the prepreparation of imines. Here, we report a photocatalytic protocol for synthesizing α-amino ketones directly from aldehydes and amines. This one-pot reaction proceeds smoothly in the presence of the photocatalyst tetrabutylammonium decatungstate (TBADT) and catalytic amounts of HBr. Aldehydes serve as both precursors for in situ imine formation and subsequent acylating agents. Hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) photocatalysis exhibits excellent two-stage compatibility, allowing the transformation under mild and simple conditions. This strategy avoids the prepreparation and isolation of imines, providing an atom- and step-economical route for the convenient synthesis of α-amino ketones.

item.title: Ammonium Chloride and Peroxide: A Metal‐Free Aqueous Strategy for Oxime Synthesis
item.description:
A metal-free aqueous strategy using NH4Cl/H2O2 with monoethanolamine enables oxime synthesis from carbonyls, tolerating 55 substrates (up to 93% yield) and gram-scale production, providing a green, cost-effective approach.


A metal-free, aqueous protocol enables the synthesis of oximes from carbonyls using NH4Cl and H2O2. A radical mechanism involving in situ hydroxylamine generation bypasses the use of unstable salts. Monoethanolamine (MEA) serves as an essential additive, facilitating the conversion of 55 substrates with yields up to 93%. The practicality is underscored by a room-temperature gram-scale synthesis that requires no chromatographic purification, establishing a cost-effective and environmentally benign alternative for oxime production.

item.title: Front Cover: Efficient Synthesis of Cannabinoid Acids (Eur. J. Org. Chem. 42/2026)
item.description: The Front Cover highlights the transformation of Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (Δ9-THC) into Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinolic acid (Δ9-THCA), symbolizing the transition from a well-known psychoactive cannabinoid to a compound of growing pharmaceutical interest. The darker imagery surrounding Δ9-THC evokes cannabis and its psychoactive properties, while the brighter motifs associated with Δ9-THCA represent health, mindfulness, and therapeutic applications. Positioned at the center, the molecular structures depict the key chemical transformation achieved in this study. In their Research Article, K. Nakamura, H. Takahashi and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/ejoc.70860) provide an efficient synthetic route to cannabinoid acids from their corresponding cannabinoids, facilitating future investigations into the medicinal potential of these compounds.

item.title: Recent Advances in Functional Group Transpositions in Arenes and Heteroarenes
item.description:
Recent advances in functional group transposition in arenes and heteroarenes are reviewed. Representative strategies, including transition-metal-enabled dissociation–recombination sequences, carbocation-mediated processes, photochemical heterocycle isomerizations, and multistep relay approaches, are discussed. Current limitations and future opportunities for the development and application of these transformations are also highlighted.


Functional group transpositions in arenes and heteroarenes constitute a powerful tool in organic synthesis, enabling access to synthetically elusive compounds. Classical aromatic rearrangements, such as the Smiles, Claisen, and Bamberger reactions, allow positional reorganization but inevitably leave a residual substituent at the original ipso carbon, thereby precluding complete transfer. In contrast, a conceptually distinct yet underdeveloped class of transformations enables genuine positional transposition, in which a substituent undergoes net positional relocation within a pre-existing or newly formed aromatic framework, thereby generating a different substitution pattern in the final aromatic product. This review delineates the conceptual boundaries among these processes and organizes previously scattered examples of functional group transposition, including transition-metal-enabled dissociation–recombination sequences, carbocation-mediated processes, and multistep relay strategies, while also discussing closely related photochemical heterocycle isomerizations involving aromatic ring reconstruction as complementary strategies for positional editing. These advances highlight new opportunities to overcome intrinsic site-selectivity limitations in aromatic synthesis.

item.title: Unorthodox Applications of Diethylaminosulfur Trifluoride and its Analogs in Organic Synthesis
item.description:
Unorthodox applications of DAST-type reagents extend beyond classical deoxyfluorination, encompassing the synthesis of diverse fluoroalkylated scaffolds as well as nonfluorinated products, thereby expanding their synthetic utility and offering new opportunities for organic synthesis, medicinal chemistry, and drug discovery.


Diethylaminosulfur trifluoride (DAST) and related reagents are well-established, commercially available nucleophilic fluorinating agents primarily known for their effectiveness in deoxyfluorination. Beyond their conventional applications, DAST-type reagents have recently emerged as versatile tools for the synthesis of CF3S-containing compounds, fluorinated benzoxathiin derivatives, and other non-fluorine-containing molecules that hold significant interest in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and materials science. This review highlights the reactivity and expanding synthetic utility of DAST-type reagents, with a particular emphasis on their unique roles in novel chemical transformations.

item.title: Ceric Ammonium Nitrate‐Promoted C4‐Selective Geminal Dinitration of Tetrahydroacridines and Nef‐Type Conversion to 2,3‐Dihydroacridin‐4(1H)‐Ones
item.description:
Ceric ammonium nitrate enables catalyst-free, C4-selective gem-dinitration of tetrahydroacridines through benzylic C(sp3)–H functionalization under neutral conditions. The resulting gem-dinitro derivatives undergo a DBU-promoted Nef-type transformation to provide valuable 2,3-dihydroacridin-4(1H)-ones. Mechanistic studies support a sequential radical nitration pathway and identify key intermediates involved in the denitrative conversion.


A catalyst-free, ceric ammonium nitrate (CAN, (NH4)2[Ce(NO3)6])-promoted, C4-selective gem-dinitration of 1,2,3,4-tetrahydroacridines has been developed via benzylic C(sp3)–H functionalization. Acting as both an oxidant and a nitrating reagent, CAN enables the regioselective synthesis of 4,4-dinitrated tetrahydroacridines in moderate-to-good yields with broad functional group tolerance. The resulting gem-dinitro products undergo an efficient DBU-mediated Nef-type transformation to furnish 2,3-dihydroacridin-4(1H)-ones. Mechanistic investigations, including radical trapping and intermediate isolation experiments, support a sequential radical-mediated gem-dinitration pathway and identify a vinyl nitro intermediate in the subsequent Nef-type transformation. To the best of our knowledge, this study represents the first example of a Nef-type conversion of gem-dinitro compounds into 2,3-dihydroacridin-4(1H)-ones.

item.title: Activation of Meso‐AmidoBODIPYs for Mild Pd‐Catalyzed Cross‐Coupling With Boronic Acids
item.description:
Meso-functionalization of the BODIPY core has been achieved using the bis-acetylamido group. Such a functional group was easily installed at the meso-BODIPY position and exhibited excellent reactivity in a Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling reaction with (Het)aryl boronic acids. This finding complements other Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions to functionalize the BODIPY meso position, which use either halogens or the methylsulfanyl group as electrophilic components.


A mild and operationally simple method for the synthesis of meso-arylBODIPYs enabled by a geometrically activated bis-acetamidoBODIPY is described. The new meso-bis-acetamidoBODIPY enables Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling at room temperature with a variety of arylboronic acids, affording a family of 17 meso-arylBODIPYs in moderate to good yields (20%–90%) within short reaction times. Computational studies revealed that the bis-acetamidoBODIPY exhibits the longest N─C8 bond and a large distortion angle (89.7°), approaching full orthogonality. These structural features explain its use as an activated platform for meso-functionalization through Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling. The optical properties of the meso-bis-acetamidoBODIPY were evaluated, highlighting the role of the meso-substituent nature and its geometric arrangement on the photophysical properties compared with the previously reported 8-aminoBODIPY and 8-acetamidoBODIPY analogs.

item.title: Aryl Triazenes From N,N‐Dialkylformamide and Aryldiazonium Salts
item.description:
Herein, we report a simple and efficient room-temperature synthesis of 1-aryl-3,3-dialkyl triazenes using N,N-dialkylformamides as both solvent and dialkylamine source.


Triazenes are valuable nitrogen-containing motifs with applications in medicinal and synthetic chemistry. Herein, we report a simple and efficient room-temperature synthesis of 1-aryl-3,3-dialkyl triazenes using N,N-dialkylformamides as both solvent and dialkylamine source. The transformation proceeds under mild conditions with broad functional-group tolerance, including heteroaryl substrates, affording the desired triazenes in moderate to good yields. Mechanistic investigations suggest a nucleophilic attack of N,N-dialkylformamide on diazonium salts through the O atom, followed by deformylation, with formic acid and acetic acid identified as byproducts. The synthetic utility of the protocol is further demonstrated through gram-scale synthesis. This operationally simple and scalable method offers a practical approach for the preparation of structurally diverse triazenes.

item.title: A Photoredox Keck Allylation Reaction Using Riboflavin as the Radical Initiator
item.description:
An efficient Keck allylation using Riboflavin Tetraacetate (RFTA) and blue LED light as the radical initiator is reported. The method is effective with both primary and secondary α-chloro and α-bromoketones as well as esters. Additionally, this procedure requires only 5 mol% of photocatalyst, unlike the standard 20 mol% of AIBN typically employed in this type of reaction.


An efficient Keck allylation using Riboflavin Tetraacetate (RFTA) and blue LED light as the radical initiator is reported. The method is effective with both primary and secondary α-chloro- and α-bromoketones as well as α-iodo- and α-bromoesters. Additionally, this procedure requires only 5 mol% of photocatalyst, unlike the standard 20 mol% of AIBN typically employed in this type of reaction.

item.title: NADH and Nonnatural Dihydronicotinamides (NAH) as Reagents in Organic Synthesis and Catalysis
item.description:
NADH and synthetic 1,4-dihydronicotinamides (NAH) are versatile redox reagents that extend beyond biological hydride transfer. This review highlights their development as nonenzymatic reagents in organic synthesis, from polar to radical reactivity and ultimately to applications in complex biological environments.


NADH is a universal redox cofactor in life. NADH and synthetic N-substituted 1,4-dihydronicotinamides (NAHs) are versatile hydride, hydrogen-atom, and electron donors, with diverse applications in nonenzymatic chemistry. This review surveys the historical development and modern applications of NADH and related NAHs as reagents in organic synthesis, spanning polar hydride-transfer and radical pathways, including SET and HAT processes, as well as emerging applications in complex biological environments. Overall, these developments highlight the potential of dihydronicotinamides as versatile, inherently biocompatible reagents beyond their traditional roles in biology.

item.title: Stereoselective Synthesis of the Ribocitrin Trisaccharide Framework via 1,2‐cis‐α‐Selective Ribofuranosylation Using Ribofuranosyl Iodides
item.description:
Ribofuranosyl iodides enable the first stereoselective synthesis of the trisaccharide framework of ribocitrin, a natural inhibitor of dextransucrase. Sequential ribofuranosylations efficiently construct its α-d-ribofuranosyl-(1→2)-α-d-ribofuranosyl-(1→3)-d-ribofuranose framework with complete 1,2-cis-α-selectivity.


Ribocitrin, a natural product isolated from Streptomyces neyagawaensis MF980-CF1, consists of (S)-homocitric acid and a trisaccharide unit, α-d-ribofuranosyl-(1→2)-α-d-ribofuranosyl-(1→3)-d-ribofuranose. Ribocitrin exhibits inhibitory activity against Streptococcus mutans dextransucrase and is therefore considered a potential preventive agent for dental caries. Although ribocitrin exhibits promising biological activity, its structural complexity is anticipated to render chemical synthesis difficult; accordingly, neither the trisaccharide moiety nor the full molecule has been synthesized to date. In this study, we present the first successful synthesis of the trisaccharide framework of ribocitrin via 1,2-cis-α-selective ribofuranosylation using ribofuranosyl iodides as glycosyl donors. Both α-glycosidic linkages were constructed with complete 1,2-cis-selectivity. The trisaccharide structure was confirmed by comparison of the spectroscopic data of its per-O-acetylated derivative with those previously reported.

item.title: Metal‐Free [3 + 2] Cycloaddition of Vinyldiazo Compounds and N‐Aryl Benzohydrazonoyl Chlorides: Efficient and Rapid Assembly of Pyrazolines
item.description:
A metal-free [3 + 2] cycloaddition between N-arylhydrazonoyl chlorides and vinyldiazo compounds is established. This mild DCM reaction at 25 °C with K2CO3 affords functionalized pyrazolines (27 examples) in up to 99% yield, suitable for late-stage transformation.


A highly general, metal-free [3 + 2] cycloaddition of vinyl diazo compounds with in situ generated nitrile imines (from N-Aryl Benzohydrazonoyl Chlorides) has been developed, providing diazo-containing, functionally enriched pyrazoline derivatives in high yields. The reaction is proposed to proceed via nucleophilic attack of the vinyldiazo compound on the nitrilimine, followed by intramolecular conjugate addition. Notably, this methodology features mild conditions and a broad substrate scope, and its synthetic utility was further demonstrated through late-stage transformations.

item.title: Synthesis, Structural Analysis and Catalytic Activity of Stabilized Selenenyl Halides From the Reaction of 1,2‍‐Benzisoselenazoles With Carbon Electrophiles
item.description:
2-Iminoarylselenenyl halides stabilized by chalcogen bonding were synthesized efficiently through the reaction of benzisoselenazoles with carbon electrophiles. Their structure was determined from spectroscopic data and by X-ray crystallography. Evaluation of their catalytic glutathione oxidase/peroxidase activity revealed a strong influence of the substitution pattern.


The synthesis of selenenyl halides stabilized by chalcogen bonding was accomplished by the reaction of benzisoselenazoles with a variety of carbon electrophiles under thermal activation. The X-ray structures of five of these derivatives resulting from the oxidative addition of the carbon–halogen bond exhibited a stabilization by a Se–N interaction. These selenenyl halides react with organomagnesium reagents by substitution at the selenium center delivering a diarylselenide. The peroxidase and oxidase activities of the stabilized selenenyl halides were measured by UV–visible spectroscopy demonstrating the strong influence of the nitrogen substituent on the catalytic activities.

item.title: Non‐Diazo Approach to Functionalized Hydroxamate Through Formal Reductive O─H Bond Insertion Reaction of Hydroxamic Acids
item.description:
Late-stage functionalization of hydroxamic acids is achieved by P(III)-mediated reaction with α-keto esters in a reductive O─H bond insertion process. This diazo-, base-, and transition-metal-free method permits the incorporation of a complex hydroxamic acid motif into the α-position of the ester using a deoxygenative umpolung strategy.


In this study, an efficient approach is investigated for accessing hydroxamates via the P(III)-mediated O─H bond insertion reaction of hydroxamic acid with α-keto esters. The key to success was determined by the in situ generation of Kukhtin–Ramirez adducts, which are useful carbene surrogates, thereby achieving diazo-, metal-, and base-free O─H bond insertion reactions. The mild reaction conditions, excellent functional group tolerance, useful synthetic transformations, and successful modification of drug molecules demonstrate the utility and practicality of this method.

item.title: One‐Pot Metal‐Free Synthesis of 3‐Substituted 4‐Hydroxyisocoumarins via Oxa‐Hauser–Kraus Reaction of Sulfonyl Phthalide With Glyoxal Derivatives
item.description:
A [4 + 2] annulation of sulfonyl phthalide with aryl glyoxal gives ready access to 3-acyl-4-hydroxyisocoumarins under mild, scalable, and transition metal-free conditions and supported by DFT calculations.


The [4 + 2] Hauser–Kraus (H–K) annulation strategy has been employed for the first time for the synthesis of 4-hydroxyisocoumarins. This method involves reaction of sulfonyl phthalide with aryl glyoxal under mild conditions (Cs2CO3, THF, rt) to generate 3-acyl 4-hydroxyisocoumarin derivatives. Good substrate scope, scalability, and further transformations of the products have been demonstrated. Calculation of highest occupied molecular orbital–lowest unoccupied molecular orbital energies, electrophilicity and nucleophilicity indices, as well as transition state energies by density functional theory provided insights into the probable mechanism of the reaction and the observed selectivity.

item.title: Ring Expansion of Carbocycles via Heteroatom‐Enabled Skeletal Editing
item.description:
This review summarizes recent advances in the ring expansion of carbocycles via nitrogen- and oxygen-atom-enabled skeletal editing, highlighting diverse mechanistic paradigms.


Carbocycles serve as fundamental scaffolds in a wide range of biologically active molecules and functional materials. Traditional synthetic transformations predominantly target peripheral functional groups, while the emerging paradigm of skeletal editing enables direct remodeling of molecular carbon backbones. Among these strategies, heteroatom insertion has become a powerful approach to access high-value heterocycles. In this review, we summarize recent progress (2020–2025) in ring expansion of carbocycles via nitrogen- and oxygen-atom-enabled skeletal editing, with an emphasis on the mechanistic paradigms of diverse strategies including transition-metal catalysis, photochemical/electrochemical activation, radical relay cascades, and cation-driven rearrangements. These methods enable selective incorporation of N or O atoms into inert C─C bonds, providing efficient access to diverse N- and O-heterocycles. We also discuss the current challenges in this field, such as the development of general catalytic systems, expansion of unactivated substrate scope, and the lack of efficient insertion strategies for other heteroatoms, and provide an outlook on future development to offer insights for programmable skeletal editing and functional molecule design.

item.title: Copper‐Catalyzed Borylative Dearomatization of Internal Alkynes With Pyrimidinium Salts and Diborons
item.description:
A three-component borylative dearomatization reaction of alkynes with B2pin2 and pyrimidinium salts is reported. The reaction features broad substrate scope using CuCl/AmPhos as the precatalyst, yielding boryl alkenyl 1,2-dihydropyrimidines as the products in moderate-to-high yields. Scale-up reactions and further transformations of the products are also demonstrated.


A three-component borylative dearomatization reaction of alkynes with B2pin2 and pyrimidinium salts is herein reported. The reaction features broad substrate scope (up to 40 examples) using CuCl/AmPhos as the precatalyst, yielding a series of boryl alkenyl 1,2-dihydropyrimidines as the products in moderate-to-high yields. Scale-up reactions and further transformations of the products are also demonstrated.

item.title: A Synthetic Journey Toward Functional N‐Amidophenyl‐Substituted Hexaaza[16]paracyclophanes
item.description:
N-amidophenyl-substituted hexaaza[16]paracyclophanes can be synthesized via a convergent and efficient pathway, combining Ullmann and Buchwald–Hartwig coupling reactions. In accordance with simpler triarylamine molecules, these macrocyclic structures exhibit interesting light-induced self-assembling properties.


Conjugated macrocycles hold great promises for applications as photo- and electroactive materials. In particular, aza-[1 n ]paracyclophane was recently described to reach high electrical conductivity in single-crystal devices due to their tubular assemblies. However, the self-assembly of these macrocycles in solution and in thin films remains a challenge. Our group reported recently that properly-designed hexaaza[16]paracyclophane molecules can self-assemble in nanotubular structures which can delocalize electrons both through bond within the macrocycle and through space along the supramolecular structure. Nevertheless, accessing these macrocyclic molecules with lateral amide moieties is not straightforward. In this paper, we report the various synthetic strategies we designed to access N-amidophenyl-substituted hexaaza[16]paracyclophane using Cu-catalyzed Ullmann coupling and Pd-catalyzed Buchwald–Hartwig reactions as key steps. The synthetic sequences were designed to reach exclusively 6-membered macrocycles, to limit purification processes to classical column chromatographies, and to provide ~100 mg scale quantities. The optimized synthetic route allowed to study the light-responsive properties of a 6-membered triarylamine-based macrocycle, following procedures originally developed for simpler triarylamine molecules.

item.title: Desulfurative Tandem Cyclization of 1,6‐Enynes and Thiols via Photoredox Catalysis: Access to Polysubstituted Piperidines
item.description:
A photoredox-driven radical cascade transforms 1,6-enynes and thiols into densely substituted piperidines via sequential CS cleavage, cyclization, and a hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) process.


A visible-light photoredox-catalyzed radical cascade cyclization of 1,6-enynes 1 with thiols 2 has been developed, enabling the efficient synthesis of polysubstituted piperidines 3 in good to excellent yields with high regioselectivity. Mechanistically, the reaction proceeds through a desulfurative/cyclization/hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) cascade, and features broad functional group compatibility, a wide substrate scope, high bond-formation efficiency, and scalability to gram-scale synthesis.

item.title: Iridium Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydrogenation of 5‐Methylene‐Benzosuberanes
item.description:
Asymmetric hydrogenation of 5- methylene-benzosuberanes using Ir-PHOX catalysts is reported. Investigation of catalyst structure–activity relationships drove the design of Ir–NoaPHOX, a novel catalyst engineered to suppress an undesired isomerization pathway. This catalyst eliminated pressure-dependent selectivity, allowing efficient hydrogenation under low H2 pressure. As a complementary system, Ir–PepPHOX-tBu delivered up to 92% ee at high H2 pressures, the best reported to date.


Asymmetric hydrogenation of 5-methylene-benzosuberanes using iridium-PHOX catalysts is reported. While the P-stereogenic ligand PepPHOX- t Bu afforded an unprecedented 92% ee for the parent substrate, competitive isomerization was found to erode selectivity. Investigation of catalyst structure–activity relationships enabled the rational design of Ir–NoaPHOX, a novel catalyst engineered to suppress this undesired isomerization pathway. Because its selectivity is independent of reaction pressure, the Ir–NoaPHOX catalyst enables efficient hydrogenation under low-pressure conditions. A range of derivatives was successfully reduced using both catalytic systems: Ir–NoaPHOX for robust low-pressure performance and Ir–PepPHOX- t Bu for maximum enantioselectivity working at 50 bar pressure.

item.title: Dimeric Cu(I) Hydride‐Catalyzed Alkene Hydrogenation and Imine Olefination: Mechanistic Insights Into Stereocontrol
item.description:
Density functional theory studies show that the dinuclear CuH complex promotes direct outer-sphere hydrogen migration to form INT1a. INT1a then adds nucleophilically to the imine (R2), a step mediated by KOpyr, which both stabilizes the negative charge on the imine nitrogen and coordinates to the Bpin oxygen—rigidly restricting Ca─Cc rotation and preorganizing the system for antielimination. The Z-alkene has a much higher isomerization barrier (ΔΔG ‡ = 3.6 kcal/mol) than the E-isomer, making interconversion thermodynamically and kinetically inaccessible.


This work employs density functional theory to elucidate the mechanism of CuH-catalyzed reductive cross-coupling between activated alkenes and imines for stereoselective C═C bond formation. Computational analysis reveals that dinuclear CuH complexes are not only thermodynamically more stable than their mononuclear analogues but also feature a sterically congested coordination environment that enforces an outer-sphere hydrogen migration pathway—enabling direct formation of the key anionic intermediate INT1a. INT1a then undergoes nucleophilic addition to the imine (R2), a step critically facilitated by potassium pyridin-4-olate (KOpyr), which simultaneously stabilizes the developing negative charge on the imine nitrogen and coordinates to the Bpin oxygen in the ensuing intermediate INT3. Conformational reorganization via Ca─Cc bond rotation in INT3 generates a well-defined, low-energy geometry that preorganizes the system for antielimination, thereby ensuring stereospecific E-olefin formation and underpinning the high diastereoselectivity observed experimentally. Furthermore, this study identifies a cooperative electronic role of the Bpin group in R1 during C═C bond activation and demonstrates that cis–trans isomerization of the E-alkene product is both thermodynamically disfavored and kinetically inaccessible under dinuclear CuH catalysis, thereby providing a rigorous, mechanism-grounded theoretical rationale for the experimentally stereochemical fidelity.

item.title: Photochemical CF3 Radical Generation: A Spin Trapping/Electron Paramagnetic Resonance and In Situ 19F Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Study
item.description:
The rate of production of the trifluoromethyl radical under photoredox catalysis conditions was studied by NMR and EPR using in situ irradiation. Eighteen compounds (sulfoniums, sulfoximines, hypervalent iodine structures) were studied.


Trifluoromethyl (CF3) radicals, generated under photoredox catalysis, are valuable tools for introducing CF3 groups into organic molecules, significantly altering their physical, chemical, and biological properties. Although reagents, like the Umemoto and Togni compounds, are widely used to introduce CF3 groups, the details of how they generate CF3 radicals are not well understood. In this article, we study the reactivity of 18 different CF3-donating reagents using two methods: spin trapping-electron paramagnetic resonance (ST/EPR) spectroscopy and in situ 19F nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). ST/EPR measures how quickly CF3 radicals are released by detecting their reaction with the spin trap 2-methyl-2-nitrosopropane (MNP), forming MNP-CF3 adducts. In parallel, 19F NMR monitors how the reagents are consumed and which products are formed during trifluoromethylation of alkenes. Notably, the observed reactivity trends differ between the two techniques, likely due to differences in reaction environments and side reactions such as CF3I formation. The comparison between each reagent must therefore be limited to the values determined by each analytical technique, EPR or NMR. This study provides nevertheless new insights into how CF3 radicals are generated and how the structure of the reagent influences its reactivity.

item.title: Chiral Copper(II) Complex‐Catalyzes Site‐Selective Monofunctionalization of Levoglucosan Analogs
item.description:
A chiral copper-catalyzed strategy for the site-selective functionalization of levoglucosan and its analogs is reported. Using CuCl2 in combination with a chiral bis(oxazoline) ligand, selective functionalization of the O2 or O4 hydroxyl group was achieved, with the regioselectivity controlled by the ligand configuration. The method enables the introduction of various protecting groups and extends to fluorinated levoglucosan and an aminosugar analog. Complementary zinc-mediated conditions proved more effective for the functionalization of an iminosugar analog. Furthermore, a reaction sequence combining selective tosylation, epoxide formation, Payne rearrangement, and azide ring opening provides access to structurally diverse azidosugars, including 3-azido-3-deoxy-d-galactose, a valuable intermediate for the synthesis of galectin inhibitors. This work establishes chiral copper catalysis as a useful approach to the site-selective modification of carbohydrate scaffolds and expands the synthetic versatility of levoglucosan-derived building blocks.


In this work, we report the development of a chiral copper-catalyzed, site-selective monofunctionalization of levoglucosan and analogs. This strategy employs CuCl2 in combination with a BOX ligand to achieve regioselective functionalization at the O2 or O4 positions. The method proved effective with a range of electrophiles, exhibiting optimal performance for the regioselective installation of benzyl and tosyl groups. The protocol was also successfully applied to an aminosugar analog. However, in the case of an iminosugar analog, functionalization mediated by a zinc diamine complex afforded superior results. Moreover, an unprecedented reaction sequence enabled the selective synthesis of complex azidosugars, including the rapid preparation of the key intermediate 3-azidogalactose. Overall, this approach represents a rare and valuable example of copper catalysis applied to the selective functionalization of carbohydrates.

item.title: Expanding the [2.2]Paracyclophane Framework: A New Synthetic Entry to π‐Extended Derivatives
item.description:
A new aryne-based route provides access to π-expanded [2.2]paracyclophanes, including anthracenophane and tetracenophane derivatives. Beyond the synthesis itself, these shape-persistent scaffolds reveal how enforced cofacial π-systems can govern molecular packing, transannular communication, and solid-state optical behavior.


We report a complementary synthetic approach to π-expanded [2.2]paracyclophanes based on aryne annulation chemistry. The method provides access to anti-anthracenophane and new tetracenophane derivatives from a common cyclophane precursor. The resulting compounds were examined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction, optical spectroscopy, and quantum-chemical calculations. The structural studies reveal that the rigid [2.2]paracyclophane framework strongly influences molecular organization in the solid state, while the spectroscopic data demonstrate substantial electronic communication between the cofacially arranged acene units. The calculations support the experimental observations and provide insight into the electronic structure and aromaticity of these π-expanded systems. This work broadens the synthetic chemistry of acenophanes and highlights their potential as shape-defined building blocks for functional organic materials.

item.title: Mechanochemical and Sonochemical Green Multicomponent Semisynthesis of Masticadienonic Acid Analogs
item.description:
Improved synthesis of natural product analogs via AES-promoted IMCR strategies.


Isocyanide-based multicomponent reactions (IMCRs) have emerged as efficient tools for the semisynthesis of natural product analogs, offering greener, faster, and more efficient compared to conventional multistep approaches. In this study, masticadienonic acid (5), a triterpenoid isolated from Pistacia mexicana, was employed in Passerini three-component (P-3CR) and Ugi four-component (U-4CR) reactions for accessing α-acyloxycarboxamides (6a–e, 8a–c) and bis-amides (14a–i). Sonochemical (SC) and mechanochemical (MC) P-3CR and U-4CR green strategies were developed, contributing to the advancement of IMCR methodologies applied to synthesize natural product analogs within the framework of Green Chemistry.

item.title: Effects of Cyclopentadienyl Ligand Structure on Rhodium(III)‐Catalyzed Ortho‐C─H Arylation of Aryl Ketones
item.description:
A tailored, electron-rich, anisotropic cyclopentadienyl ligand enables rhodium(III)-catalyzed ortho arylation of aryl ketones at 80  °C using readily available arylboronic acid pinacol esters. Direct use of a cationic catalyst promotes binding of the weak ketone directing group, while scope and competition experiments reveal how ketone electronics and steric demand control reaction efficiency.


Ketones are attractive innate directing groups for C─H bond functionalization, but their weak coordination to transition metals often necessitates harsh conditions. We report a cyclopentadienyl-ligand-controlled rhodium(III)-catalyzed ortho-arylation of aryl ketones with arylboronic acid pinacol esters. Comparison of electronically and sterically differentiated ligands identified an electron-rich, anisotropic 3,4,5-trimethoxyphenyl-substituted cyclopentadienyl ligand (CpTMP*) as the most effective catalyst platform at 80 °C. A preformed cationic rhodium(III) complex containing CpTMP* afforded the model biaryl ketone in 65% isolated yield, whereas the conventional pentamethylcyclopentadienyl rhodium(III) catalyst was substantially less effective under the same conditions. The reaction accommodates electron-rich, electron-deficient, and halogenated arylboronic acid pinacol esters, together with aryl ketones bearing varied alkyl substituents, providing the corresponding biaryl ketones in yields of up to 79%.

item.title: Amphiphilic Dendrimers Based on a Thiacalix[4]arene‐Gallic Alcohol Conjugate: Synthesis, Aggregation Behavior, and Catalytic Activity in Aqueous Media
item.description:
Amphiphilic dendrimers with sulfonate (SO3Na), ethylene glycol (EG), and hydroxyl (OH) groups stabilize palladium nanoparticles (Pd NPs) through two distinct functions: surface catalysis (polar periphery) and substrate solubilization (hydrophobic thiacalix [4]arene core). The terminal group governs aggregation behavior and catalytic performance. In nitroarene reduction, OH and SO3Na derivatives excel (k app up to 0.9 min−1) due to accessible small aggregates. In contrast, EG-functionalized dendrimers achieve up to 99% conversion in aqueous Suzuki–Miyaura and Heck cross-coupling, combining high thermal stability with efficient substrate solubilization. The optimal dendrimer stabilizer depends on both reaction type and substrate hydrophobicity.


A novel family of amphiphilic dendrimers based on a thiacalix[4]arene-gallic alcohol conjugate was synthesized via Mitsunobu reaction followed by copper-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC). Three types of polar peripheral groups—sulfonate (SO3Na), oligoethylene glycol (EG), and hydroxyl (OH)—were introduced to impart hydrophilic character, while the hydrophobic thiacalix[4]arene core served as the lipophilic domain. The dendrimers were employed as stabilizers for palladium nanoparticles (Pd NPs). Nanoparticle racking analysis revealed that the terminal group critically governs aggregation behavior, with SO3Na inducing compaction, EG promoting surface aggregation, and OH disrupting pre-existing aggregates to generate a larger number of smaller particles. The Pd&R-TCA composites exhibited excellent catalytic activity in the reduction of p-nitrophenol (k app up to 0.9 min−1) and p-ethylnitrobenzene (k app up to 0.6 min−1), significantly outperforming unsupported Pd0 and Pd(OAc)2. In aqueous Suzuki–Miyaura and Heck cross-coupling, the Pd&EG-TCA system demonstrated the highest conversions (up to 99%) due to its superior thermal stability and substrate solubilization capacity, as confirmed by TEM and Orange OT tests. The activity order reversed compared with reduction reactions, highlighting that the optimal dendrimer stabilizer depends on both reaction type and substrate hydrophobicity.

item.title: Trifluoromethanesulfonyl‐Based Reagents: Novel Synthetic Strategies and Mechanistic Insights for Trifluoromethylation Transformations
item.description:
Trifluoromethylated compounds act as indispensable synthetic building blocks in the fields of agrochemicals, pharmaceuticals, and functional materials, by virtue of their tunable lipophilicity, enhanced cell membrane permeability, and superior metabolic stability. The content is organized and discussed by distinct catalytic modes, covering photoredox catalysis, electrochemical catalysis, metal-free catalysis, and transition-metal-catalyzed trifluoromethylation protocols. This review summarizes the advances achieved between 2016 and 2026, with a dedicated focus on trifluoromethanesulfonyl-mediated transformations, and provides a comparative analysis of various CF3 reagents.


Trifluoromethylated compounds act as indispensable synthetic building blocks in the fields of agrochemicals, pharmaceuticals, and functional materials, by virtue of their tunable lipophilicity, enhanced cell membrane permeability and superior metabolic stability. The distinctive physicochemical characteristics of the trifluoromethyl group have stimulated tremendous research interest in developing efficient, site-selective, and scalable synthetic methodologies for the trifluoromethylation of diverse organic molecular skeletons. Over recent years, trifluoromethanesulfonyl-derived trifluoromethylating reagents have arisen as versatile, bench-stable, and easily accessible CF3 sources, facilitating the development of numerous green, atom-economic, and mild synthetic strategies to access structurally varied trifluoromethylated compounds and functional molecular scaffolds. This review systematically summarizes the advances in catalytic trifluoromethylation reactions enabled by trifluoromethanesulfonyl derivatives, which are categorized into four main types: photoredox catalysis, electrochemical catalysis, metal-free catalysis, and transition-metal catalysis for trifluoromethylation transformations.

item.title: Photocatalytic Pyridylation of Cyanopyridines With Benzyl and Alkyl Dihydropyridines: Divergent Reactivity and Mechanistic Insights
item.description:
A visible-light-induced coupling of cyanopyridines with alkyl- and benzyl-substituted 1,4-dihydropyridines (DHPs) provides an efficient route to C4-alkyl pyridines under transition-metal-free conditions. Mechanistic studies reveal distinct reactivity patterns for benzyl and alkyl DHPs, while cyclic voltammetry and Jiang's dual-parameter Hammett analysis identify the key factors governing substrate compatibility and the turnover-limiting step.


The divergent reactivity of benzyl- and alkyl-substituted 1,4-dihydropyridines (DHPs) in the photocatalytic pyridylation of cyanopyridines has been investigated. A visible-light- and sunlight-driven coupling protocol was developed, providing a practical transition-metal-free route to C4-alkyl pyridines with broad substrate scope, gram-scale applicability, and utility in the synthesis of Ifenprodil. Mechanistic studies revealed that benzyl and alkyl DHPs require distinct photocatalyst/solvent combinations for efficient coupling. Cyclic voltammetry measurements established a redox-matching model that governs substrate compatibility, while Jiang's dual-parameter Hammett analysis identified fragmentation of the DHP radical cation as the turnover-limiting step. These findings provide new mechanistic insight into DHP-mediated photoredox transformations and offer a useful framework for understanding and predicting the reactivity of DHP-derived radical processes.

item.title: Cyanation of Dihydropyrrolo[2,1‐a]isoquinoline With Phenylacetonitrile
item.description:
An efficient cyanation reaction for the direct cyanation of dihydropyrrolo[2,1-a]isoquinoline with phenylacetonitrile has been described. This reaction is performed in DMF using CuI as the promoter. Various substrates are well compatible, affording the corresponding products in moderate-to-good yields. This work provides an operationally simple approach to the construction of Lamellarin scaffolds.


An efficient cyanation reaction for the direct cyanation of dihydropyrrolo[2,1-a]isoquinoline with phenylacetonitrile has been described. This reaction is performed in DMF using CuI as the promoter. Various substrates are well compatible, affording the corresponding products in moderate-to-good yields. This work provides an operationally simple approach to the construction of Lamellarin scaffolds.

item.title: In Situ Generation of (Dichloroiodo)benzene From PhI(OAc)2 and SOCl2: Application to the Synthesis of Chlorinated 1,3‐Dicarbonyl and Aromatic Compounds
item.description:
A highly efficient and practical method for in situ generation of PhICl2 utilizing (diacetoxyiodo)benzene [PhI(OAc)2] and thionyl chloride (SOCl2) has been developed. Highly selective a-mono-chlorination of 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds was achieved using the in situ-generated PhICl2 under mild conditions. Mechanistic studies confirmed in situ generation of PhICl2 from PhI(OAc)2 and SOCl2. The chlorination of aromatic rings further demonstrated the versatility of this protocol.


(Dichloroiodo)benzene (PhICl2) is a powerful reagent used in chlorination, but its practical utility is often limited by instability and hazardous methods of synthesis. We developed a straightforward and efficient protocol for in situ generation of PhICl2 utilizing (diacetoxyiodo)benzene [PhI(OAc)2] and thionyl chloride (SOCl2). Mechanistic studies confirmed in situ generation of PhICl2 from PhI(OAc)2 and SOCl2. Highly selective α-mono-chlorination of 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds was achieved using the in situ-generated PhICl2 under mild conditions; α,α′-di-chlorinated products were successfully obtained by adjusting the reagent stoichiometry. The chlorination of aromatic rings further demonstrated the versatility of this protocol.

item.title: Transition Metal‐Free C(sp2)─Ge Bond Construction and Downstream Functionalization
item.description:
Organogermanes combine the advantages of other tetrels such as silicon or tin without their respective downsides in terms of stability and reactivity. This Perspective describes both the transition metal-free formation of C(sp2)─Ge bonds and the subsequent functionalizative degermylation reactions to access organic compounds of interest. Further applications comprise, among others, radiolabeling of aryls, drug discovery and doping of PAHs with boron atoms.


Organogermanes have emerged as versatile, orthogonal handles for transition metal-free electrophilic ipso-substitutions. This review highlights protocols enabling the synthesis of aryl- and vinylgermanes and their downstream functionalization through halodegermylation and acyldegermylation to form new C─X and C─C bonds, as well as C─B bonds via borodegermylation. These reactions deliver aryl halides, ketones, and organoboranes with high chemo- and regioselectivity, orthogonal to boronic esters and silanes. Applications span traceless solid-phase synthesis of π-oligomers and the preparation of BN-fused polycyclic aromatics for optoelectronic materials. These transition metal-free transformations emphasize the synthetic potential of organogermanium compounds in complex molecule assembly and advanced functional materials.

item.title: Rigidification of 7‐Aminocoumarins Bearing Electron‐Withdrawing Groups Increases Emission Intensity in Polar Environments
item.description:
The heretofore unknown amino-coumarin-lactams maintain strong emission in polar aprotic solvents. The combined experimental and computational study revealed that blocking free rotation of electron-withdrawing substituent at position 4 plays a key role in the fate of these molecules in the excited state.


A set of structurally unique coumarins possessing an amino group at position 7 and lactam ring fused to the coumarin lactone ring were synthesized for the first time via Pechmann reaction. The photophysics of these new polarized donor–acceptor dyes were compared with those of structural analogs bearing an ester and amide groups at position 4, revealing significant differences in absorption/emission maxima, solvatofluorochromism and emission intensity. Emission of coumarin-lactams is blue in cyclohexane and orange in MeOH, whereas coumarin-esters emit cyan light in cyclohexane and red light in MeOH. Crucially, rigidification of coumarin-lactams’ skeleton combined with replacement of ester with amide functionality has a profound effect on emission intensity decrease in polar solvents: even in acetonitrile, fluorescence quantum yields are still around 50%. Computational studies probed the nature of the key excited states of all dyes and enabled us to venture the hypothesis that blocking free rotation of electron-withdrawing group at position 4 is responsible for controlling non-radiative dissipation of energy in more polar solvents.

item.title: Gold‐Catalyzed Cyclization of Indole‐Tethered Alkynes Enabling Synthesis of Exocyclic Alkenyl Tetrahydrocarbazoles
item.description:
An efficient gold-catalyzed intramolecular cyclization of indole-tethered alkynes using AgNTf2 as an additive has been developed, which provides bioactive exocyclic alkenyl tetrahydrocarbazoles with up to 85% yield. Control experiments and DFT studies indicate that the reaction proceeds via a 6-exo-dig cyclization pathway, with gold acetylide complexes as key intermediates and HE as a base.


A gold-catalyzed intramolecular cyclization of indole-tethered alkynes using Hantzsch ester (HE) and AgNTf2 as additives has been developed, providing diverse functionalized exocyclic alkenyl tetrahydrocarbazoles in good to excellent yields. Control experiments and DFT studies indicate that the reaction proceeds via a 6-exo-dig cyclization pathway, with gold acetylide complexes as key intermediates and HE serving as a base. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions, shows broad functional-group tolerance, and is amenable to scale-up. Selected tetrahydrocarbazole products also exhibited moderate antifungal activity against two forest pathogenic fungi.

item.title: Electrochemical Synthesis of Sulfur(VI) Compounds
item.description:
Sulfur(VI) motifs are widely found in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and materials science. Electrochemical synthesis offers a sustainable route to these valuable scaffolds by replacing conventional oxidants with electric current. This review highlights recent advances in the electrochemical synthesis of diverse S(VI) compounds under mild and practical conditions.


Electrochemical synthesis is emerging as a green and versatile platform for sulfur(VI) chemistry, using electric current to replace or minimize the use of stoichiometric oxidants and to access high-valent sulfur under generally mild conditions. This review highlights recent (2020–2025) electrochemical methods for the preparation of key S(VI) motifs, including sulfonyl fluorides, sulfones, sulfonate esters, thiosulfonates, sulfoximines, and sulfonimidoyl fluorides. Emphasis is placed on the transformation of simple S-containing precursors in straightforward undivided or flow cell setups under mild conditions, highlighting electrosynthesis as a sustainable tool for constructing and editing sulfur(VI) scaffolds relevant to medicinal chemistry, agrochemicals, and materials science.

item.title: Click Bioconjugation of Aza‐BODIPY Fluorophores to LfcinB Peptides for Improved Biocompatibility
item.description:
Click bioconjugation attaches NIR aza-BODIPY fluorophores to LfcinB-derived anticancer peptides via CuAAC and thiol-maleimide chemistry. Conjugates exhibit improved predicted solubility while retaining strong NIR absorption (703–730 nm). Peptide-aza-BODIPY conjugates induce apoptotic morphology in HeLa cancer cells.


Near-infrared (NIR) organic fluorophores have emerged as promising for biomedical imaging and theragnostics, offering deep-tissue penetration and reduced background interference. However, poor aqueous solubility and limitations in photostability, biocompatibility, and targeting hinder in vivo applications. Similarly, antimicrobial and anticancer peptides exhibit proteolytic instability and rapid clearance. This study addresses these issues by covalently bioconjugating aza-BODIPY fluorophores with LfcinB-derived peptides (RRWQWR, RWQWRWQWR) using CuAAC and thiol-maleimide click chemistries. Two strategies were compared: (i) CuAAC between azide/alkyne-functionalized partners, and (ii) Michael addition with cysteine-containing peptides and AZB-maleimide. Bioconjugation significantly improved water solubility (calculated LogP 5.3–5.5 → 1.1–4.2; LogS −8.2 → −2.2/−3.7) while preserving NIR photophysical properties (λ ab s = 703–730 nm). In silico ADMET analysis provided preliminary support for favorable predicted absorption-related properties and metabolic stability. Thiol-maleimide constructs showed superior predicted solubility, lower mutagenicity, and more favorable synthetic accessibility than CuAAC analogs. Phase-contrast microscopy of HeLa cells revealed characteristic apoptotic morphology (cell rounding/shrinkage, membrane association) with blue staining reflecting aza-BODIPY localization. In parallel, P12 induced caspase activation in flow cytometry assays, providing preliminary evidence of caspase-associated apoptotic activity. Collectively, these platforms provide a basis for the further development of NIR probes, although their in vivo performance remains to be established experimentally.

item.title: Copper‐Catalyzed One‐Pot Approach to 6‐Membered Sultams From Vinyl Sulfonamide Using Methanol as C1 Building Block
item.description:
A CuBr2-catalyzed oxidative coupling of vinyl sulfonamides with methanol efficiently constructs taurultams under ambient, air-tolerant conditions. Serving dually as solvent and sustainable C1 source, methanol enables diverse 6-membered sultams to be delivered in high yields with broad functional group tolerance, offering an operationally simple, scalable, and practical approach to taurultam synthesis.


A CuBr2-catalyzed one-pot oxidative coupling of vinyl sulfonamides with methanol has been developed for the efficient construction of taurultams. Methanol functions dually as solvent and C1 source, while H2O2 serves as a benign oxidant. The reaction proceeds under ambient conditions without inert atmosphere requirements, demonstrating excellent functional group tolerance and delivering diverse sultams in high yields. This operationally straightforward protocol demonstrates that copper-catalyzed activation of methanol enables its utilization as a sustainable C1 building block for taurultam synthesis, establishing a scalable and practical route to 6-membered sultam scaffolds.

item.title: Ring‐Opening Cyclization (ROC) of Aziridines With 2‐(2‐Bromophenyl)‐1H‐Benzimidazoles: Rotamer Analysis and Synthesis of Benzimidazole‐Fused 1,4‐Benzodiazepine
item.description:
A two-step synthetic route to benzimidazole-fused 1,4-benzodiazepines in good to excellent yields via base-mediated nucleophilic ring opening of activated aziridines followed by copper-mediated intramolecular C–N cyclization is developed. Unexpected rotamerism in the ring-opening intermediates was supported by VT-NMR and further substantiated by DFT calculations, providing insight into their conformational dynamics.


We report a novel strategy for the synthesis of benzimidazole-fused 1,4-benzodiazepine derivatives in up to excellent yields via base-mediated nucleophilic ring-opening of activated aziridines with 2-(2-bromophenyl)-1H-benzimidazoles, followed by a Cu-powder-mediated intramolecular C–N cyclization reaction. Conformational isomerism in the ring-opening products due to restricted rotation around the N─C bond was observed. These rotameric compounds were characterized through variable-temperature NMR (VT-NMR) and further supported by DFT calculations.

item.title: Strategic Formation of Indoles Using Phenyl Hydrazine as a Key Reagent
item.description:
Indole formation from phenylhydrazine bridges classical Fischer indolisation with transition-metal-catalyzed and tandem methodologies. This review covers Rh(III), Ru(II), and Co(III)-catalyzed C─H activation, oxidative annulation, and redox-neutral coupling, along with alkyne, alcohol, ester, ketone, carboxamide acid, alkene, cyclic ether, and aldehyde routes to diversely substituted indoles.


Indole formation from phenylhydrazine represents one of the most versatile and mechanistically rich domains in heterocyclic synthesis, bridging classical Fischer indolisation with emerging transition-metal-catalyzed and tandem methodologies. Transition-metal catalysis, such as Rh(III), Ru(II), and Co(III) complexes, has been used for C─H activation, oxidative annulation, and redox-neutral coupling that yield high selectivity and diverse functional group-containing indoles. Moreover, hydroformylation-assisted Fischer reactions, ligand-controlled rearrangements, and acid-promoted condensations have demonstrated controllable C2/C3-substitution and regioselectivity across alkenes, aldehydes, and cyclic precursors. Collectively, these advancements establish phenyl hydrazine as a robust scaffold for the synthesis of multifaceted indoles. This review encompasses alkyne, alcohol, ester, ketone, carboxamide acid, alkene, cyclic ether, and aldehyde routes to diversely substituted indoles.

item.title: [Metal–(Nitrogen and/or OxygenPhosphorus‐Based Ligand)]‐Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydrogenation of β‐Amido β‐Substituted Acrylic Esters and Phosphoro Analogs: A Practical Literature Overview
item.description:
 and/or OxygenPhosphorus-Based Ligand)]-Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydrogenation of β-Amido β-Substituted Acrylic Esters and Phosphoro Analogs: A Practical Literature Overview"/>

Transition-metal-complex-catalyzed asymmetric CC hydrogenation of β-amido β-substituted acrylic esters, phosphonates, and phosphine oxide analogs has been reviewed featuring the application therein of enantiopure (N and/or O)P-monodentate, bis(N and/or O)P-, and (N and/or O)P,P-bidentate ligands.


The advent in catalysis of enantiopure (N and/or O)P-monodentate, bis(N and/or O)P-, and (N and/or O)P,P-bidentate ligands is recounted. In particular, their transition-metal-complex-enabled enantioselective CC hydrogenation of archetypal β-amido β-(alkyl or aryl)-vinylcarboxylic esters, phosphonates, and phosphine oxide analogs is reviewed. The efficient P-ligands are juxtaposed with their reported attained enantioselectivity per substrate alongside the screening conditions. Additional literature pertaining to the asymmetric hydrogenation of the said phosphonates, employing enantiopure diphosphine ligands, is included.

item.title: Photochemical Synthesis of Dihydropyrido[1,2‐a:3,4‐b′]diindole Derivatives
item.description:
A visible-light-induced cyclization of N-(substituted benzoyl)-tetrahydro-β-carbolines was developed to construct dihydropyrido[1,2-a:3,4-b’]diindole scaffolds. This metal-free, p-toluenesulfonic acid (PTSA)-assisted reaction proceeds under 425 nm LED light in N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) in up to 84% yield, tolerating F, Cl, CF3, and OCH3 substituents and fused rings. Mechanistic studies support a photoexcited H-shift/radical coupling/dehydration pathway.


Herein, we report a photochemical method for the intramolecular cyclization of N-(substituted benzoyl)-1-substituted-1,2,3,4-tetrahydro-β-carbolines. This transformation relies on photoexcitation of the substrate itself in the absence of external photocatalysts, with catalytic p-toluenesulfonic acid (PTSA) facilitating the cyclization process.
