This reaction provides a straightforward and practical approach for the synthesis of dihydro-pyrido[1,2-a:3,4-b′]diindoles. We investigate the substrate scope by varying substituents at the R 2 and R 9 positions of the starting materials. A variety of dihydro-pyrido[1,2-a:3,4-b′]diindoles were successfully synthesized in moderate to excellent yields (up to 84%). Substrates bearing alkyl, aryl, polysubstituted, and fused-ring moieties are well tolerated. Furthermore, the synthetic practicability of this protocol is validated by a gram-scale reaction.

item.title: Modifying Catalytic Sustainability in Renaud Catalysts: Hints From Aromaticity, Conceptual DFT, and Steric Mapping
item.description:
Replacing precious-metal hydrogenation catalysts with sustainable iron systems is becoming a central challenge in catalysis. This predictive computational study reveals how rational redesign of Knölker-type iron complexes dramatically enhances catalytic performance. By tuning cyclopentadienone substituents and annulated rings, activation barriers are significantly reduced, toward highly efficient, greener hydrogenation catalysis.


Catalytic hydrogenation is a key transformation in the chemical and pharmaceutical industries, traditionally relying on noble-metal catalysts such as palladium, ruthenium, and iridium. However, the scarcity, high cost, and environmental concerns associated with these metals have motivated the search for sustainable alternatives based on abundant first-row transition metals. Among them, Knölker-type iron complexes have emerged as promising candidates for efficient hydrogenation catalysis. This predictive study investigates how structural modifications of the cyclopentadienone ligand of the Renaud ligand and annulated-ring framework affect the catalytic activity of iron-based hydrogenation catalysts. Particular attention is devoted to the catalyst activation process and the rate-determining hydrogenation step. Catalyst activation occurs through CO ligand dissociation promoted by trimethylamine-N-oxide, generating the active iron species. The hydrogenation step, involving molecular hydrogen transfer, represents the highest energetic barrier in the catalytic cycle, although protic solvents such as ethanol or water can facilitate this process. The computational results demonstrate that appropriate substituent and ring modifications substantially lower the activation barriers, leading to improved catalytic efficiency. Parameterization by different techniques was performed to understand reactivity trends and interaction patterns.

item.title: Advances in NN Bond Formation: Mechanistic Diversity and Emerging Catalytic Strategies
item.description:
N Bond Formation: Mechanistic Diversity and Emerging Catalytic Strategies"/>

This review provides an overview of recent advances in NN bond formation through thermal, photochemical, and electrochemical strategies. Key approaches, including oxidative dehydrogenative coupling, reductive coupling, enzymatic catalysis, and metal-catalyzed nitrene transfer, are discussed with emphasis on reaction design, mechanistic insights, and synthetic applications.


The nitrogen–nitrogen (NN) bond is ubiquitous in organic compounds, yet efficient synthetic strategies for the direct construction of NN bonds remain challenging. Well-known approaches, such as oxidative dehydrogenative coupling (ODC) and reductive coupling (RC), have provided valuable routes for forming NN linkages. Nitrene transfer strategies emerged as a complementary and increasingly versatile platform. The distinct electronic structures of classical closed-shell nitrenoids (Fischer- and Schrock-type), open-shell nitrene radical intermediates, and photochemically generated nitrene species primarily govern NN bond-forming selectivity. The use of electrochemical, photochemical, and biocatalytic approaches continues to expand the scope of sustainable synthetic chemistry. This review summarizes recent advances in ODC, RC, nitrene transfer chemistry, photochemical, electrochemical, and enzymatic approaches for NN bond formation, with particular emphasis on reaction design, mechanistic insights, and synthetic applications.

item.title: Synthesis of Symmetrical Secondary Amines From Aqueous Ammonia and Primary Alcohols Catalyzed by an Iridium Complex
item.description:
Ammonia gets a second life: ammonia is cheap and abundant, but selectively obtaining a single class of amine from it remains challenging. An iridium catalyst bearing an N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) ligand now converts aqueous ammonia and primary alcohols into symmetrical secondary amines via N,N-dialkylation, with no organic solvent and only water as the byproduct, offering practical access to a class of amines that has long been hard to obtain selectively.


A new catalytic system for N,N-dialkylation of aqueous ammonia with various primary alcohols to afford symmetrical secondary amines selectively has been developed. An iridium catalyst bearing an N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) ligand exhibits high performance for this reaction. This catalytic system is based on the borrowing hydrogen strategy. The reaction proceeds without additional organic solvent and generates only water as the stoichiometric byproduct.

item.title: Construction of Diarylmethane‐ and Triarylmethane‐Based Unnatural Amino Acid Motifs via Pd(II)‐Catalyzed Diastereoselective sp3 C–H Arylation
item.description:
Diastereoselective incorporation of diarylmethane (DAM) and triarylmethane (TAM) moieties in the backbone of amino acid molecules via directing group-aided site-selective sp3 C–H functionalization and synthesis of novel DAM- and TAM-based unnatural amino acid motifs, including phenylalanine, norvaline, norleucine, leucine, 2-aminobutyric acid, and alanine, are reported.


This paper reports the incorporation of diarylmethane (DAM) and triarylmethane (TAM) moieties in the backbone of amino acid molecules via directing group-aided site-selective sp3 C–H functionalization. In general, DAM and TAM are found in numerous natural products, bioactive compounds, agrochemicals, and material chemistry. Given the importance of DAM and TAM molecules, this work reports the expansion of the library of DAM- and TAM-based unnatural amino acid motifs. N-Phthaloyl carboxamides of amino acids possessing 8-aminoquinoline directing group were subjected to the Pd(II)-catalyzed β-C(sp3)–H activation and arylation using DAM- and TAM-based iodoaryls as the coupling partners. This process has led to the synthesis of novel DAM- and TAM-based unnatural amino acid motifs, including phenylalanine, norvaline, norleucine, leucine, 2-aminobutyric acid, and alanine. Then, synthetic transformations, including the removal of the directing and the phthalimide protecting groups, and the synthesis of free amino group-containing DAM- and TAM-incorporated amino acid motifs, were shown. Examples of peptide compounds containing the DAM or TAM moiety and unnatural amino acid derivatives were synthesized. Furthermore, we have presented preliminary studies on the metal-sensing properties of representative DAM and TAM molecules synthesized in this work.

item.title: Visible‐Light‐Mediated Hydro‐Pentafluoroethylation of Terminal Alkenes With Chloropentafluoroethane
item.description:
Chloropentafluoroethane (CFC-115, R-115), a regulated C2F5-containing refrigerant, is repurposed as a pentafluoroethyl radical precursor through visible-light photoredox/trimethylamine–borane halogen atom transfer. The resulting radical enables metal-free hydro-pentafluoroethylation of terminal alkenes to access C2F5-substituted alkanes.


Direct utilization of fluorocarbon feedstocks as fluoroalkyl radical precursors provides an attractive approach to value-added organofluorine compounds, yet selective activation of their fluorine-deactivated C─Cl bonds remains challenging. Herein, we report a visible-light-driven, metal-free hydro-pentafluoroethylation of terminal alkenes using chloropentafluoroethane (CFC-115, R-115) directly as the C2F5 source. A trimethylamine–borane-mediated halogen atom transfer strategy enables efficient activation of the strong C─Cl bond of R-115 under mild conditions, generating pentafluoroethyl radicals for subsequent alkene functionalization. Terminal alkenes furnished the corresponding C2F5-substituted products in 60%–98% isolated yield, and a 5.0 mmol reaction delivered gram-scale amount of product in 69% yield. This work establishes regulated R-115 as a viable pentafluoroethyl radical precursor and illustrates a visible-light strategy for converting a fluorocarbon feedstock into value-added organofluorine compounds.

item.title: Copper‐Catalyzed Cascade Thiolation‐Cyclization of o‐Bromochalcones With Ethyl Thioglycolate: Access to 3‐Styryl Benzo[b]thiophenes
item.description:
A copper-catalyzed regioselective thiolation of o-bromochalcones with ethyl thioglycolate for constructing 3-styrylbenzo[b]thiophenes in good to excellent yields with broad substrate scope is presented.


A copper-catalyzed regioselective thiolation of o-bromochalcones with ethyl thioglycolate has been developed for constructing ethyl (E)-3-styrylbenzo[b]thiophene-2-carboxylates in good to excellent yields (up to 84%) with broad substrate scope and good functional-group tolerance. This approach highlights the versatility of the methodology, providing a diverse series of 3-styryl and π-conjugated benzo[b]thiophenes (>20 examples). Structural confirmation of this novel chemical framework was achieved through a detailed 2D NMR analysis. The transformation proceeds through copper-catalyzed C─S bond formation, followed by intramolecular condensation and cyclization. Gram-scale synthesis and late-stage modification further validate the scalability of this method and its value for synthetic diversification. Overall, this straightforward and regioselective approach offers a practical route for synthesizing structurally diverse ethyl (E)-3-styrylbenzo[b]thiophene-2-carboxylate derivatives.

item.title: Electrochemical Driven Decarboxylative Fluorination of α‐Ketoacids
item.description:
An electrocatalytic decarboxylative fluorination of α-ketoacids has been developed for the synthesis of acyl fluorides. Anodic oxidative decarboxylation generates acylium intermediates, which are subsequently trapped by fluoride ions.


Acyl fluorides are valuable acyl transfer platforms owing to their unique reactivity and stability; however, their preparation often requires specialized fluorinating reagents, metal catalysts, or stoichiometric oxidants. Herein, we report an electrocatalytic decarboxylative fluorination of α-ketoacids for the synthesis of acyl fluorides using inexpensive triethylamine trihydrofluoride (Et3N·3HF) as both the fluoride source and supporting electrolyte. Mechanistic studies support a pathway involving anodically generated acyl radicals that undergo further oxidation to acylium ions before fluoride trapping. This protocol features mild reaction conditions, broad substrate scope, excellent functional-group tolerance, and gram-scale applicability, providing a practical, economical, and sustainable approach to acyl fluorides from readily available α-ketoacids.

item.title: Nucleophilic Vinylic Substitution of 2,2‐Diaryl‐Substituted 1‐Chlorovinyl p‐Tolyl Sulfoxides With Alkynyllithiums
item.description:
A nucleophilic vinylic substitution (SNV) reaction of 1-chlorovinyl p-tolyl sulfoxides with alkynyllithiums provides a direct route to conjugated enynes. The transformation proceeds with stereochemical retention. Experimental studies and DFT calculations support a concerted SNVπ mechanism.


Nucleophilic vinylic substitution (SNV) reactions of 2,2-diaryl-substituted 1-chlorovinyl p-tolyl sulfoxides with alkynyllithiums yield 2-chloro-substituted conjugated enynes via Csp─Csp2${\mathrm C}_{\mathrm{sp}^2}$ bond formation. Sulfoxide bearing two 4-chlorophenyl groups at the 2-position is highly reactive toward various alkynyllithiums. The reaction proceeds with configuration retention, which suggests that it follows an SNVπ mechanism. DFT calculations support a concerted SNVπ pathway involving simultaneous C─C bond formation and C─S bond cleavage, with an activation barrier of 18.7 kcal mol–1.

item.title: Front Cover: Nucleophilic Vinylic Substitution of 2,2‐Diaryl‐Substituted 1‐Chlorovinyl p‐Tolyl Sulfoxides With Alkynyllithiums (Eur. J. Org. Chem. 41/2026)
item.description: SN2 reactions at vinyl carbons are generally difficult. In contrast, 2,2-diaryl-1-chlorovinyl p-tolyl sulfoxides undergo nucleophilic vinylic substitution (SNV) with alkynyllithiums to afford enynes. The Front Cover represents the high energy barrier of conventional SNV as a mountain and the lower transition-state energy of the sulfoxide system as a saddle. More information can be found in the Research Article by T. Kimura and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/ejoc.70866).

item.title: Copper‐Catalyzed Substrate‐Controlled Assembly of 1,3,5‐Triazines From Aldehydes and Ammonium Acetate
item.description:
From aldehydes to nitrogen-rich heterocycles: a copper-catalyzed cycloaromatization of aldehydes with ammonium acetate provides symmetrical and unsymmetrical 1,3,5-triazines directly from simple feedstocks. The reaction proceeds through nitrile intermediates and displays substrate-controlled divergence, affording 3,5-disubstituted pyridines from aldehydes possessing at least two α-hydrogens.


A copper-catalyzed assembly of symmetrical and unsymmetrical 1,3,5-triazines directly from readily available aldehydes and ammonium acetate is reported. The use of ammonium acetate as a simple nitrogen source enables access to structurally diverse 2,4,6-trisubstituted 1,3,5-triazines without the need for prefunctionalized nitrogen-containing building blocks. A broad range of aromatic, heteroaryl, fused-ring, and metallocene-derived aldehydes undergo the transformation under operationally simple conditions. Mechanistic studies suggest the involvement of radical intermediates and nitrile species in the triazine-forming pathway. Interestingly, the reaction outcome is influenced by the nature of the aldehydic α-carbon: whereas aldehydes lacking sufficient α-hydrogens undergo the triazine-forming cycloaromatization pathway, tested aldehydes bearing at least two α-hydrogens follow an alternative pathway to afford 3,5-disubstituted pyridines. The reaction is readily scalable and provides a practical approach to nitrogen-rich heterocycles from simple aldehyde feedstocks.

item.title: Carbon‐Supported Catalytic Systems Assembled by π–π Interactions
item.description:
This review explores the noncovalent immobilization of organic and organometallic catalysts on carbonaceous supports through π–π interactions, highlighting its potential to enhance catalyst recovery, recyclability, and the sustainability of organic synthesis. It surveys applications in achiral and enantioselective transformations, examining the influence of support properties on catalytic performance and comparing heterogeneous and homogeneous systems. Finally, it discusses the opportunities and current limitations of this strategy for developing efficient and sustainable catalytic processes.


The immobilization of molecular catalysts on carbonaceous supports through noncovalent π–π interactions has emerged as an attractive strategy for developing more sustainable catalytic processes. Carbon-based materials combine high surface areas, chemical and thermal stability, and tunable surface properties, while enabling the reversible immobilization of π-conjugated catalysts, notably through pyrene–surface interactions. This approach offers potential advantages in catalyst recovery, recycling, product purification, and, in the case of metal complexes, the reduction of metal contamination. Moreover, the proximity of immobilized catalytic species may provide opportunities for cooperative or tandem catalytic processes. This review surveys the use of carbonaceous allotropes—including graphene, reduced graphene oxide, carbon nanotubes, fullerenes, carbon black, charcoal, and magnetic carbon-based materials—as supports for organometallic and organic catalysts. Particular attention is devoted to their applications in achiral and enantioselective transformations, catalyst stability and recyclability, and, where available, comparisons with the corresponding homogeneous systems. The influence of support characteristics, including material quality, aggregation state, dispersion, and purification, is also considered as a critical factor affecting catalytic performance and the comparability of reported results. By bringing together these developments, this review highlights the opportunities and current limitations of noncovalent catalyst immobilization on carbonaceous supports for sustainable organic synthesis.

item.title: Photochemistry of N‐Phenyl Benzonaphthothiophene and Dinaphthothiophene Sulfoximines
item.description:
The sequential photorelease of nitrenes and atomic oxygen [O(3P)] from N‑phenyl benzonaphthothiophene and dinaphthothiophene sulfoximines is a rare photochemical phenomenon in which two reactive intermediates can be released from a single chromophore.


The sequential photorelease of nitrenes and atomic oxygen [O(3P)] is a rare photochemical phenomenon by which two reactive intermediates can be released from a single chromophore. This reactivity has been previously demonstrated in dibenzothiophene (DBT) sulfoximines. We expand the chromophore framework to benzonaphthothiophene (BNT) and dinaphthothiophene (DNT) N-phenyl sulfoximine systems to investigate how π-system extension and electronic effects influence photochemical behavior. Benzonaphthothiophene derivatives bearing electron-donating and electron-withdrawing substituents were synthesized to probe electronic effects on photoactivity. Photochemical characterization revealed that DNT-based scaffolds exhibit significantly enhanced reactivity, with quantum yields of sulfoxide formation approaching threefold higher than those observed for unsubstituted BNT analogs. Electron-donating/withdrawing group-substituted BNT derivatives showed moderate increases in quantum yield, indicating that electronic tuning provides incremental improvements relative to chromophore expansion. Spectroscopic measurements show that DNT derivatives display pronounced redshifted absorption and emission profiles with lower singlet excited‑state energies, consistent with increased π‑delocalization. Mechanistic studies, including nitrene trapping, triplet sensitization, and time‑resolved kinetics, support a stepwise photodecomposition pathway involving initial S─N cleavage to form nitrene intermediates followed by S─O bond cleavage to generate O(3P). Overall, these findings demonstrate that chromophore extension is a more effective strategy than simple electronic substitution for enhancing reductive photodeimination of aryl sulfoximines.

item.title: Heptacyclic Skeleton Construction in the Total Synthesis of Hetisine‐Type C20‐Diterpenoid Alkaloids
item.description:
The densely bridged skeletons of hetisine-type C20 diterpenoid alkaloids pose demanding synthetic challenges. This minireview compares cycloaddition, radical cyclization, and skeletal rearrangement strategies used to assemble these frameworks. Particular attention is paid to nitrogen incorporation, functional-group placement, and the relationship between rapid skeletal construction and overall route efficiency.


Hetisine-type C20-diterpenoid alkaloids (DAs) are a prominent subclass of C20-diterpenoid alkaloids, renowned for their exceptionally complex N-fused caged architecture and bicyclo[2.2.2]octane core. Their highly strained 6/6/6/6/5/5/5 heptacyclic framework features at least 9 contiguous stereocenters, 3 all-carbon quaternary centers, and a distinctive N–C6 bridge, presenting formidable challenges for chemical synthesis. In this minireview, we provide a comprehensive overview of all reported total syntheses of hetisine-type DAs, highlighting the strategic innovations that have enabled the efficient assembly of the heptacyclic framework and N-fused cage-like architecture. This minireview provides strategic insights into the synthesis of hetisine-type DAs and may facilitate the development of efficient synthetic approaches to other complex polycyclic natural products.

item.title: Bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (TFSI)‐Catalyzed Regioselective N1‐Alkylation of Benzotriazoles
item.description:
A metal-free, TFSI-catalyzed protocol enables the highly regioselective N 1-alkylation of benzotriazoles with diazo compounds. With 20 mol% catalyst loading, N 1-alkylated products are obtained in up to 90:10 N 1:N 2 selectivity under mild conditions, and the process is readily scalable to the gram scale without loss of yield or selectivity.


A metal-free, bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (TFSI)-catalyzed protocol has been developed for the good regioselective N 1-alkylation of benzotriazoles with diazo compounds. Employing only 20 mol% TFSI as the catalyst, this method delivers N 1-alkylated products (N 1:N 2 up to 90:10) with a broad scope of substrates under mild conditions. The reaction is readily scalable to the gram scale without compromising yield or selectivity.

item.title: Reductive Deletion of Endocyclic Oxygen Atom in 1,2‐Oxazine N‐Oxides to Access N‐Hydroxypyrrolidines
item.description:
Single-atom ring-editing strategies have emerged as a powerful tool for the diversification of molecular libraries through the remodeling of key heterocyclic scaffolds. Here, we introduce a novel reductive ring contraction of 1,2-oxazine N-oxides that achieves the formal deletion of the endocyclic oxygen atom, delivering valuable N-hydroxypyrrolidines.


Single-atom ring-editing strategies have emerged as a powerful tool for the diversification of molecular libraries through the remodeling of key heterocyclic scaffolds. The 1,2-oxazine core represents an ideal platform for implementing single heteroatom deletion/swapping strategies, which lead to five-membered O- or N-heterocycles with varying levels of saturation. Here, we introduce a novel reductive ring contraction of 1,2-oxazine N-oxides that achieves the formal deletion of the endocyclic oxygen atom, delivering synthetically valuable N-hydroxypyrrolidines. This process operates under mild reductive conditions with the NaBH3CN/TsOH system via an unprecedented multistep ring opening/ring reconstruction sequence. The introduction of a recyclable chiral auxiliary enables a practical asymmetric variant, providing a route to enantioenriched N-hydroxypyrrolidines.

item.title: Two‐Step, Telescopic Synthesis of Unsymmetrical Urea via Integration of Denitrogenative Methyl N‐Arylcarbamates Formation and Their Aminolysis
item.description:
A transition metal- and isocyanate-free telescopic strategy for the synthesis of unsymmetrical ureas is presented. The method combines oxidative denitrogenative radical alkoxycarbonylation of amines with direct nucleophilic substitution, enabling seamless amine-to-urea conversion without intermediate isolation. Broad substrate scope, gram-scale synthesis, pharmaceutical applications, and mechanistic studies demonstrate the versatility and sustainability of this approach.


Unsymmetrical ureas are valuable structural motifs in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials; however, their synthesis often relies on toxic reagents, transition metals, or isocyanate intermediates, resulting in poor sustainability and limited scalability. Herein, we report an unconventional, transition metal-free telescopic synthesis of unsymmetrical ureas through oxidative denitrogenative radical alkoxycarbonylation of amines using methyl carbazates, followed by direct base-promoted aminolysis. Unlike previous carbamate-based approaches that require isocyanate formation or are restricted to carbamate synthesis alone, this strategy enables seamless amine-to-urea conversion without intermediate isolation or isocyanate involvement. The protocol employs an inexpensive TBHP/I2 system, exhibits broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance, and is applicable to gram-scale synthesis, pharmaceutical intermediates, and late-stage drug functionalization. Mechanistic studies support a sequential radical denitrogenative coupling/nucleophilic substitution pathway, establishing the first telescopic application of denitrogenative chemistry of hydrazides for the construction of valuable urea frameworks.

item.title: Convergent Total Syntheses of Anti‐Diol Diastereomers of Tonkinelin Toward Its Absolute Structure Assessment
item.description:
A concise convergent total synthesis of (17S,18R,36S)-tonkinelin and its diastereomer (17R,18S,36S)-tonkinelin has been achieved by combination of asymmetric dihydroxylation of a cis-olefin, Wittig olefination, ring-closing metathesis, and chemoselective diimide olefin reduction.


The stereoselective syntheses of (17S,18R,36S)-tonkinelin and its diastereomer (17R,18S,36S)-tonkinelin via a convergent strategy have been achieved. The strategy involved the stepwise construction of two key fragments—a chiral ester-derived phosphonium salt and a requisite aldehyde for a convergent Wittig olefination. These are the anti-diol isomers of tonkinelin and were synthesized to gain more insight on the absolute configuration of the natural isolate. Asymmetric dihydroxylation of cis-olefin, Wittig olefination, ring-closing metathesis, and chemoselective diimide olefin reduction were key steps employed. The synthesis of all four diastereomers helped to establish the natural isolate to have the (17S,18S,36S) absolute configuration.

item.title: 1,1,1,3,3,3‐Hexafluoroisopropanol‐Enhanced Redox‐Mediated Diels–Alder Cycloadditions of Anthracenes: Experimental and Computational Study
item.description:
Hexafluoroisopropanol (HFIP), added even in small quantities, greatly enhances AgIISO4-redox-induced Diels–Alder reaction between anthracenes and chalcones with up to 25-fold increase of yield or with over 100-fold shortening of reaction time. The plausible action of HFIP is the enhancement of the solubility of oxidized diene (anthracene)+• resulting from the strong solvation of accompanying inorganic sulfate-containing counterions.


This study presents a detailed study on the effect of presence of 1,1,1,3,3,3-hexafluoroisopropanol (HFIP) on redox-mediated Diels–Alder reaction between anthracenes and chalcones induced by oxidation by AgIISO4. The introduction of even a minimal amount, 1% (v/v), of HFIP is shown to have a significant effect on the reaction rate. The optimization of the DA reaction protocol in the examined system leads to substantial rise of yields (up to 25 times) or reduction of reaction time (up to >100 times), allowing facile synthesis of cycloadducts from poorly active reactants which are otherwise difficult to obtain. Experimental and computational results point to the role of HFIP as the enhancement of solubilization of (Anth)+• through complexation of the [AgISO4]− counterion, while the alcohol itself does not interact strongly with radical cations involved in the reaction.

item.title: Polyaromatic Fused Zn–Salen as a Photocatalyst for Carboxylation of Terminal Alkynes Using CO2 as a C1‐Source
item.description:
B–N fused phenanthroimidazolyl zinc–salen/1,8-diazabicycloundec-7-ene system as a photocatalyst is presented for the synthesis of propiolic acids/esters under mild CO2 pressure and temperature. The protocol exhibits broad functional-group tolerance with good to excellent yields.


Blue LED-driven conversion of CO2 into value-added products under mild conditions remains a primary challenge in sustainable synthetic methods. Herein, we report a B–N fused phenanthroimidazolyl Zn–salen complex catalysed protocol for carboxylation of terminal alkynes using CO2 at atmospheric pressure under blue LED irradiation. A wide range of aromatic and heteroaromatic alkynes were screened and efficiently converted to their corresponding propiolic acids with good to excellent yields using 1,8-diazabicycloundec-7-ene (DBU) as a base and DMSO as a solvent. Subsequent alkylation of propiolic acids enables a wide array of structurally diverse propiolate esters, revealing its electrophile compatibility. Mechanistic studies indicate that continuous light irradiation is crucial for efficient conversion, and also reveal that DBU plays a dual role in C(sp)─H proton abstraction and CO2 activation. This work reflects the potential of Zn–salen complex as an efficient photocatalyst for mild, sustainable, and greener utilization of CO2.

item.title: Synthesis of Borylated Compounds Through Decarboxylative and Decarbonylative Reactions
item.description:
As carboxylic acids are commercially available, naturally abundant, structurally diverse and bench-stable, their transformation into boronate esters or boronic acids is highly attractive. This review gives a comprehensive overview of the various strategies of radical decarboxylative and decarbonylative borylation and alkylation of carboxylic acid derivatives, including transition-metal-catalyzed, photocatalyzed, and thermally activated reactions.


Organoboronates and organoboronic acids are important and versatile building blocks in organic synthesis, in materials science, and in medicinal chemistry as carboxylic acid bioisosteres. The most employed reactions to generate organoboronates are transmetallation and hydroboration of olefins. However, as carboxylic acids are commercially available, naturally abundant, structurally diverse, and bench-stable, their direct transformation into boronate esters or boronic acids is very attractive. This review highlights the recent developments in the direct decarboxylative, decarbonylative borylations, and alkylations of carboxylic acid derivatives. This review intends to be a practical tool for selection of suitable reaction conditions for specific transformations. The parameters facilitating the decarboxylation process are highlighted as a function of the substrate structure. The reviewed methodologies span from transition-metal catalysis to photocatalysis.

item.title: Modular Synthesis of Di‐ and Triazadibenzoazulenes by a Cross‐Coupling/Cycloisomerization Strategy
item.description:
Two series of regioisomeric di- and triazadibenzoazulenes were prepared from dihalogenated imidazo[1,2-a]pyridines and imidazo[1,2-a]pyrazines.


Imidazo[1,2-a]pyridines and imidazo[1,2-a]pyrazines are important nitrogen-containing heterocycles with applications in medicinal and materials chemistry. Herein, we report a regioselective synthetic strategy for the preparation of novel diaza- and triazadibenzoazulene derivatives through sequential Pd-catalyzed Sonogashira and Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling reactions, followed by Brønsted acid-promoted cycloisomerization. The sequence of the cross-coupling reactions enabled selective access to distinct regioisomeric intermediates, which were efficiently converted into fused seven-membered azaazulene frameworks under optimized conditions. The methodology offers a broad substrate scope and affords the target compounds in good-to-excellent yields.

item.title: Synthesis of 5‐Trifluoromethyl‐1,2,4‐Triazoles via Palladium‐Catalyzed [4 + 1] Oxidative Annulation of Trifluoroacetimidohydrazides and Isocyanides
item.description:
A palladium-catalyzed [4 + 1] oxidative annulation of trifluoroacetimidohydrazides and isocyanides has been achieved for the facile construction of biologically important 1,2,4-triazoles with both trifluoromethyl and amino functionality in moderate-to-excellent yields.


A Pd-catalyzed aerobic oxidative annulation of trifluoroacetimidohydrazides and isocyanides has been developed, offering an efficient and straightforward access to valuable 1,2,4-triazoles with both trifluoromethyl and amino functionality. The reaction proceeds smoothly with catalytic Pd(OAc)2 without an additional ligand, which features simple operation, low catalyst loading, high efficiency, and scalability. In this transformation, isocyanide serves as the C1 and amino source.

item.title: Emergent Atropisomerism Through Diels–Alder Reactions of Vinylallenes
item.description:
Cycloaddition-induced geometric reorganization transforms achiral vinylallenes into atropisomeric styrenes. Conformational flexibility governs atropisomerization barriers, thermodynamic preferences, and configurational stability.


Atropisomeric styrenes remain comparatively underdeveloped because configurational stability about the C(sp2)C(sp2) bond is difficult to achieve and often relies on substantial preinstalled steric congestion. We report a conceptually distinct approach in which atropisomeric styrenes emerge through Diels–Alder reactions of substituted vinylallenes with N-methylmaleimide. In these reactions, cycloaddition-induced geometric and hybridization changes generate a sterically hindered styrenyl atrop-axis as a direct consequence of bond formation rather than through direct construction of a congested C(sp2)C(sp2) bond. Simultaneously, the reactions generate stereogenic ring junction centers that convert the two orientations about the atrop-axis into diastereomeric relationships, giving rise directly to distinguishable atropisomeric cycloadducts from achiral precursors. Experimental and computational studies reveal that atropisomerization barriers are governed not simply by steric congestion about the atrop-axis, but by conformational flexibility of the fused bicyclic framework. Unexpectedly, gem-dimethyl substitution at the exocyclic alkene lowers the atropisomerization barrier through ground-state destabilization arising from enhanced cyclohexene puckering and reduced distortion required to reach the rotational transition structure. Extension of this design principle enabled the preparation of configurationally stable atropisomeric styrenes that could be separated chromatographically and analyzed independently at ambient temperature.

item.title: Regio‐ and Stereoselective Synthesis of Spirooxindole–Pyrrolidine Hybrids Through 1,3‐Dipolar Cycloaddition: The Development of Potent α‐Glucosidase Inhibitors
item.description:
A novel series of spirooxindole–pyrrolidine hybrids was synthesized via a regio- and stereoselective 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition. Bromine-substituted derivatives showed high α-glucosidase inhibitory activity. Structural elucidation confirmed stereochemistry, revealing that the electronic nature of arylimine substituents influences diastereoselectivity and provides insights for designing more potent future inhibitors.


A novel series of spirooxindole–pyrrolidine hybrids was synthesized and evaluated for their potential as α-glucosidase inhibitors. These compounds were obtained via a regio- and stereoselective 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition reaction between arylimines and an isatin-derived alkene. Structural elucidation by NMR spectroscopy and single-crystal X-ray diffraction enabled unambiguous stereochemical assignment and provided insight into the diastereoselectivity of the reaction. Furthermore, the stereochemical outcome was found to be influenced by the electronic nature of the substituents on the arylimine moiety, offering valuable insight into the reaction mechanism. Among the synthesized compounds, bromine-substituted analogues exhibited α-glucosidase inhibitory activity over 12-fold greater than that of the reference drug acarbose, highlighting their potential as lead compounds for the development of next-generation inhibitors.

item.title: Mechanistic Insights Into Catechin Epimerization: Interplay of Deprotonation and Quinone Methide Stabilization
item.description:
Catechin epimerization is governed by the interplay between the acidity of the 4′-hydroxyl group and stabilization of a quinone methide intermediate. Experimental studies combined with DFT calculations reveal how B-ring substitution and C3 substituents control epimerization profiles, providing a molecular basis for understanding catechin transformations during thermal processing.


Catechin epimerization occurs during thermal processing of tea and can influence its bioactivity and nutritional properties. However, the structural factors governing epimerization behavior remain incompletely understood. In this study, we systematically investigated the effects of chemical structure on epimerization using native catechins and a series of model compounds under heating conditions relevant to food processing. The time-dependent changes in peak area ratios during epimerization and the equilibrium ratios were evaluated by HPLC analysis, and the observed trends were interpreted using density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The results demonstrate that epimerization is influenced by both the acidity (pK a) of the 4′-hydroxyl group and stability of the quinone methide intermediate, and is governed by the interplay between these factors. Electronic effects on the B-ring were found to influence deprotonation of the 4′-hydroxyl group, whereas intramolecular hydrogen-bonding interactions contributed to stabilization of the quinone methide intermediate. Substituents at the C3 position further influence both epimerization profile and equilibrium ratio through electronic and steric effects. These findings establish a mechanistic framework for catechin epimerization and provide insight into structure–reactivity relationships in polyphenolic systems undergoing quinone methide-mediated transformations.

item.title: Visible‐Light‐Promoted Electron Donor–Acceptor‐Induced Coupling Reaction of Ketyl Radicals With Alkane
item.description:
A visible-light-promoted electron donor-acceptor (EDA) complex strategy for the generation of ketyl radicals from aryl aldehydes and their subsequent coupling reaction is reported.


A visible-light-promoted electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complex-enabled generation of ketyl radicals from aryl aldehydes and their coupling reaction is reported. This mild, photocatalyst- and transition metal-free protocol provides direct access to a variety of α,β-unsaturated compounds in moderate to excellent yields. Mechanistic studies support the formation of a key EDA complex between the aldehyde and the in situ generated enolate from DMA and t BuONa, with radical coupling as the pivotal step. This work expands the scope of EDA-mediated ketyl radical chemistry under mild conditions.

item.title: Practical One‐Pot Synthesis of Cyclic Conjugated Amides From Ketones
item.description:
Cyclic conjugated amides from simple ketones: a one-pot bromoform-mediated homologation/amidation sequence provides direct access to 20 conjugated amides, including functionalized and linear examples, in up to 91% yield.


Conjugated amides are valuable building blocks in organic synthesis; however, general access to cyclic conjugated amides remains limited, restricting their broader use in method development and complex molecule synthesis. Herein, we report a practical one-pot synthesis of cyclic conjugated amides directly from readily available ketones. The transformation employs bromoform, an amine nucleophile, and 1,8-diazabicyclo[5.4.0]undec-7-ene (DBU) and is proposed to proceed through carbene-mediated homologation followed by in situ trapping of an acyl halide intermediate. A range of cyclic ketones and primary and secondary amines are converted into the corresponding conjugated amides in moderate to very good yields, including substrates bearing protected heterocycles, ether functionality, and alkyl or aryl substituents. The method also provides access to selected linear conjugated amides from acyclic ketones, including 1,1-disubstituted derivatives.

item.title: A General Stereochemical Model for Grignard Additions to α‐Alkoxy Nitrones: Density Functional Theory Evidence for an Intrinsic α‐Chelation‐Controlled Pathway
item.description:
A comprehensive DFT conformational study of Grignard additions to α-alkoxy nitrones reveals that the reaction proceeds through a dinuclear α-chelated transition structure in which the nitrone oxygen coordinates two magnesium centers. Other common additives, such as zinc dichloride, boron trifluoride, and dimethylaluminum chloride, were also studied. Boltzmann, NCI, and distortion–interaction analyses explain the experimentally observed divergent syn/anti selectivity as the result of a subtle balance between steric and electronic effects.


Nucleophilic additions of Grignard reagents to nitrones constitute a powerful and versatile methodology for stereoselective synthesis. The ability to control and even invert diastereoselectivity through LA coordination offers unique opportunities for divergent synthetic strategies. However, the complex electronic, conformational, and coordination properties of nitrones have long hindered the development of reliable mechanistic models. By comparing competing transition structures for nucleophilic attack under different coordination scenarios, it becomes possible to rationalize both the preservation and inversion of diastereoselectivity observed experimentally and to lay the groundwork for rational design and prediction in future applications.

item.title: Front Cover: 1,1,1,3,3,3‐Hexafluoroisopropanol‐Enhanced Redox‐Mediated Diels–Alder Cycloadditions of Anthracenes: Experimental and Computational Study (Eur. J. Org. Chem. 40/2026)
item.description: The Front Cover shows how the addition a small amount of hexafluoroisopropanol (a droplet of HFIP in the picture) to the reaction mixture greatly increases the speed and the yield of cycloaddition reactions between chalcone and anthracene derivatives. The mechanism involves solubilization of the anthracene radical cation (the crab) together with the AgI(SO4)− counter anion (the piece of coral), the latter coming from the AgIISO4 oxidation reaction initiator. More information can be found in the Research Article by M. J. Jadwiszczak, P. J. Leszczyński, P. J. Malinowski and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/ejoc.70851). Artwork by Małgorzata Fürst.

item.title: Synthetic Strategies for the Construction of Cyclobutane‐Fused Heterocycles
item.description:
Cyclobutane-fused heterocycles are important motifs commonly present in bioactive compounds, recognized for their rigid 3D structures that confer unique properties. However, synthesizing these compounds remains challenging. This review discusses current methods for their synthesis, such as photochemical, metal-catalyzed, and Lewis acid-mediated [2 + 2] cycloadditions, as well as ring-closure techniques including cascade reactions and strain-release annulations.


Cyclobutane-fused heterocycles represent a distinctive class of structurally constrained scaffolds with significant relevance in natural products and medicinal chemistry. Recent advances in synthetic organic chemistry have enabled the development of diverse, increasingly efficient strategies for their construction. Among these, [2 + 2] cycloaddition-based approaches have emerged as central tools, spanning photochemical dearomative transformations of heteroarenes, olefin [2 + 2] photocycloadditions, and Lewis acid- or transition-metal-catalyzed variants, including enantioselective and visible-light-mediated processes. Alongside these approaches, complementary ring-closure strategies, including cascade processes and strain-release annulations, have also been reported in recent years, providing efficient and elegant access to cyclobutane-fused heterocycles through mechanistically distinct pathways. This review provides a critical overview of the principal synthetic strategies for constructing cyclobutane-fused heterocycles, with an emphasis on reactivity patterns, selectivity control, and mechanistic features.

item.title: Selective N‐Functionalization of Pyrazoles
item.description:
This review traces the evolution of regioselective N-functionalization strategies for pyrazoles, a key class of nitrogen heterocycles widely used in medicinal chemistry. Due to rapid tautomerism, N-functionalization often lacks selectivity, leading to poor and unpredictable regioisomeric outcomes. Recent advances in transition-metal catalysis, directing-group, radical, and skeletal-editing strategies have improved control and expanded access to diverse substitution patterns.


Pyrazoles are five-membered heteroarenes that contain two neighboring nitrogen atoms and appear in diverse functional molecule classes. One nitrogen contributes a lone-pair to the aromatic π-system, while the lone-pair of the other lies orthogonal. However, easy interconversion between tautomers of N─H pyrazoles occurs and the two forms lie close in energy to each other. As a consequence, N-functionalization reactions most commonly lead to mixtures of products in what is a well-known synthetic challenge. Demand for selective, efficient alternatives has prompted innovation of new, diverse synthetic strategies which can overcome this problem. In this review, we focus on the most recent developments in this field.

item.title: Recent Synthetic Approaches and Future Prospects of Trifluoroacetyl Compounds
item.description:
This review provides a comprehensive and critical overview of all synthetic avenues to trifluoroacetyl-containing compounds, encompassing both indirect approaches (e.g., oxidation of trifluoromethyl carbinols) and direct methods using electrophilic, radical, and building-block-type trifluoroacetylating reagents, which aims to serve as a comprehensive decision-making guide for synthetic chemists and to highlight underexplored areas ripe for future methodological innovation.


The incorporation of a trifluoroacetyl group into drug candidates has emerged as an indispensable strategy in modern pharmaceutical research. In contrast to cumbersome indirect methods, direct trifluoroacetylation using readily available reagents provides a more straightforward route. This review provides a comprehensive and critical overview of all synthetic avenues to trifluoroacetyl-containing compounds, encompassing both indirect approaches (e.g., oxidation of trifluoromethyl carbinols) and direct methods using electrophilic, radical, and building-block-type trifluoroacetylating reagents. This review aims to serve as a comprehensive decision-making guide for synthetic chemists and to highlight underexplored areas ripe for future methodological innovation.

item.title: Organic Azides in Process Chemistry: Reactivity, Hazards, and Safe Handling
item.description:
This review highlights the role of azides in pharmaceutical chemistry, in the manufacturing of modern active pharmaceutical ingredients. Extensive chemical possibilities open when the use of azides is envisaged. However, the related hazards and risks must be thoroughly addressed for a safe and robust scale-up. An overview is provided of main azide concerns, with some general strategies to tame them.


Organic azides are commonly exploited as precursors to a variety of key functional groups that are increasingly relevant in the manufacturing of active pharmaceutical ingredients. Azides allow access to complex nitrogen-rich heterocyclic structures that are responsible for the bioactive properties of numerous substances. However, organic azide intermediates and the reagents used to synthesize them are associated with relevant safety risks, due to their potential explosivity and toxicity. These problematic features can be tamed with thorough evaluation prior to scale-up and by establishing the appropriate safety measures. This review provides an overview of the synthetic relevance of azides as reagents and intermediates, with a summary of reagents used in azide formation. The second part of the review provides some general rules for their handling at various stages, from process development to subsequent industrialization. These include dos and don’ts in terms of chemical compatibility, equipment selection and refinement both at lab and plant scale, strategies for azide quenching, and waste handling. The last section is devoted to recent developments in azide chemistry handling in continuous mode.

item.title: Photocatalyst‐Free Trifluoromethylation of Indolizines Through an Electron Donor–Acceptor Complex
item.description:
A new photocatalyst-free pathway for the direct C-3-trifluoromethylation of indolizines and imidazo[1,2-a]pyridines through an electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complex is studied. This regioselective reaction supports a wide range of functional groups, indicating good versatility and robustness.


The indolizine scaffold has attracted considerable interest owing to its broad potential in medicinal chemistry. We describe a photochemical trifluoromethylation that enables direct C-3 functionalization of indolizines and imidazo[1,2-a]pyridines without the use of a photocatalyst, allowing the reaction to proceed under milder and more environmentally friendly conditions. Mechanistic investigations support the in situ formation of an electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complex. The protocol exhibits broad functional group tolerance, delivering 27 C-3 trifluoromethylated indolizine and imidazo[1,2-a]pyridine derivatives with yields up to 82%, underscoring its synthetic robustness and versatility. Overall, this methodology simplifies the access to C-3 functionalized indolizines and facilitates the exploration of new structures with potential biological relevance.

item.title: Synthesis and Studies of Phenothiazine Bridged 3‐Pyrrolyl BODIPY Dyads
item.description:
Phenothiazine-bridged bis(3-pyrrolyl BODIPY)s with distinct linkage topologies were synthesized. The α-pyrrolyl linkage enhances donor-acceptor conjugation, giving redshifted absorption/emission and a lower oxidation potential. The study establishes a linkage-sensitive structure–property relationship within bis(3-pyrrolylBODIPY) framework.


Two phenothiazine-bridged 3-pyrrolyl BODIPY dyads, 1 and 2, were synthesized through Sonogashira coupling of 3,7-diethynyl-N-methylphenothiazine with meso-(p-iodophenyl) and α-bromo 3-pyrrolyl BODIPY, respectively. Although both molecules contain identical donor and acceptor units, their linkage modes differ: Compound 1 connects through the meso-phenyl ring of 3-pyrrolyl BODIPY unit, whereas compound 2 connects through the α-position of the appended pyrrole of 3-pyrrolyl BODIPY unit. 1D and 2D NMR analyses confirmed that this topological change modifies the donor–acceptor conjugation pathway. Consequently, 2 exhibits strongly redshifted absorption and emission bands relative to 1 (638 vs. 587 nm and 685 vs. 618 nm, respectively), along with a larger Stokes shift. Both dyads show irreversible, oxidation-dominated electrochemical responses, but 2 oxidizes at a lower potential, consistent with enhanced conjugation. DFT and TD-DFT calculations attribute these differences to the smaller donor–acceptor dihedral angle and greater HOMO delocalization in 2. Overall, the NMR, optical, electrochemical, and computational results consistently support a linkage-site-dependent structure–property relationship, in which the α-pyrrolyl connection enhances donor–acceptor communication within these molecular frameworks.
